/// The Design Studio filters its `.working` pulse, its auto-pan and its Inspector subject by the
/// SELECTED kit, so a touch it cannot place in a kit is discarded. It can resolve the kit from its own
/// hydrated copy for anything it already loaded — but that misses exactly the interesting case, a
/// record written seconds ago, so the kit rides the event instead.
///
/// Reads the stored record to find `kitId`. Best-effort in the same spirit as the emit itself: a miss
/// (absent record, unreadable store, no `kitId`) degrades to the historical 5-column line rather than
/// failing, because activity signalling must never break a store mutation.
fn emit_component_activity(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, kind_is_write: bool, id: &str) {
    let kit = current_record(store, id)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|v| v.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).map(str::to_string))
        .unwrap_or_default();
    if kind_is_write {
        bsc_util::emit_ui_activity_in("component", id, &kit);
    } else {
        bsc_util::emit_ui_focus_in("component", id, &kit);
    }
}

/// The record's CURRENT stored JSON (`Value::Null` when absent), so a write can carry its change history
/// forward and diff what changed (#3568). Malformed stored JSON reads as absent (fail-safe: the write
/// still lands, just starting a fresh history rather than erroring on a corrupt row).
fn current_record(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, id: &str) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
    Ok(store.get(id)?.and_then(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&j).ok()).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null))
}

/// Stamp `value` for a write (bump `rev`, set `updatedAt` + `updatedBy`), then upsert it by `id`. The
/// single write boundary EVERY non-`set` writer funnels through (the animation authors, doctor `--fix`
/// repoints), so they all get a consistent rev bump + attribution; `writer` is the resolved tag (see
/// [`crate::record::resolve_writer`]).
fn stamped_set(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    id: &str,
    mut value: serde_json::Value,
    writer: &str,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let prior = current_record(store, id)?;
    crate::record::stamp_with_history(&mut value, &prior, writer, &crate::record::now_iso(), None);
    store.set(id, &serde_json::to_string(&value).map_err(|e| format!("set: {e}"))?)
}

/// Read the `set` payload — a single record object OR an array of them — into a `Vec`.
///
/// Two channels, identical semantics (#3373): stdin, or `--file <bare-name>` resolved inside the
/// session's sealed `$BSC_SCRATCH` dir. The file form exists because a heredoc cannot be allow-listed
/// (newlines are command separators), which left a restricted studio session unable to author at all.
/// `bsc_cli_util::read_payload` owns the resolution + the traversal defence.
fn read_set_items(noun: &str, file: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<serde_json::Value>, String> {
    let raw = bsc_cli_util::read_payload(file)?;
    let where_ = if file.is_some() { "in --file" } else { "on stdin" };
    let value: serde_json::Value =
        serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("{noun} JSON {where_} is invalid: {e}"))?;
    Ok(match value {
        serde_json::Value::Array(items) => items,
        other => vec![other],
    })
}

/// How a `set` combines the incoming record with the stored one (#4197).
///
/// The DEFAULT is a MERGE ([`crate::record::merge_over`]): unsupplied fields are preserved, and removal is
/// explicit (`--clear a,b`, or a JSON `null` in the payload). That mirrors `bsc graph impl set` after
/// #4154 — the two stores answer a partial write identically, which is the whole point: a worker told to
/// "edit the RECORD, then re-emit" (#4193) must not lose the fields its edit never mentioned, and for a
/// page whose source file is gone (`fleetpage`, since #3636) the record is the only copy.
///
/// `replace` (`--replace`) restores the verbatim whole-record write, which three callers genuinely need:
/// the app's `pushComponent`/`pushKit` bridge, `bsc ui import`, and — the load-bearing one —
/// `reconcileSeed`'s seed-authoritative path (#3723), which forces a diverged builtin back onto its seed
/// copy. Under a merge that push could never converge: a store-only field would survive every reset, so
/// the record's content hash would stay off the seed's and the reconcile would re-fire forever.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
struct WritePlan<'a> {
    replace: bool,
    clear: &'a [String],
}

/// The warning for a write that removes a field WITHOUT BEING ASKED TO (#4197) — `None` for every
/// merging write (which removes only what `--clear`/a `null` names) and for every `--replace` that
/// restates the whole record, so the common paths stay silent and the warning keeps its meaning.
///
/// It exists for the one remaining way to lose data silently: `--replace` with a partial payload. An
/// explicitly cleared field is NOT reported — the caller asked for it, and a warning about a deletion you
/// just requested is the noise that trains people to ignore the real one (the removal is still recorded
/// in the history's `dropped`, so `bsc ui log` shows it either way).
///
/// PURE so the decision is under test rather than tangled in the write loop; the caller prints it. It
/// names each field, because "this write is destructive" without a list is not actionable — the reader
/// needs to know whether it dropped `srcText` or a `folder` tag.
fn destructive_write_warning(
    id: &str,
    noun: &str,
    prior: &serde_json::Value,
    effective: &serde_json::Value,
    clear: &[String],
) -> Option<String> {
    let dropped: Vec<String> = crate::record::dropped_fields(prior, effective)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|f| !clear.iter().any(|c| c == f))
        .collect();
    if dropped.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    Some(format!(
        "warning: this write REMOVES {} field(s) from {noun} '{id}': {}. \
         --replace writes the record VERBATIM — drop --replace to MERGE (unsupplied fields are kept), \
         re-send them, or `bsc ui log {id}` to see what was there.",
        dropped.len(),
        dropped.join(", "),
    ))
}

/// The merging, stamped, version-aware `set` core (#3164/#4197): for each item, read the current stored
/// record, enforce `--if-version` (reject a stale overwrite), combine it with the stored one per `plan`
/// (a MERGE unless `--replace`), stamp (`rev+1` + `updatedAt` + `updatedBy`), upsert, and fire the
/// ui-touch hook. Returns the written ids in input order. Split out of [`cmd_set`] so the merge +
/// concurrency + stamping logic is unit-testable without a drivable stdin. `--if-version` takes a
/// SINGLE record (a lone version number is meaningless across a batch).
/// Apply a relink plan's writes (#4223) — a MERGING, stamped write of just `src`/`folder`.
///
/// Exported because the relink verb lives in `bsc-ui` (it needs the harvest, which sits a crate above
/// this one), while the write must still go through the same stamped path every other component write
/// uses — so a re-point bumps `rev`, records attribution, and lands in `bsc ui log` like any edit.
pub fn apply_relink(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, writes: &[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(None);
    set_stamped(store, writes, None, &writer, "component", Some("relink: re-point a stale src"),
                WritePlan { replace: false, clear: &[] })?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Apply a module LIFT's write — a MERGING, stamped write, so a lift bumps `rev`, records attribution
/// and lands in `bsc ui log` like any other edit.
///
/// Exported for the same reason [`apply_relink`] is: `bsc ui lift` lives in `bsc-ui` (it needs the
/// harvest, which sits a crate above this one), while the write must still go through the one stamped
/// path every component write uses.
pub fn apply_lift(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    writes: &[serde_json::Value],
    by: Option<&str>,
    note: &str,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(by);
    set_stamped(store, writes, None, &writer, "component", Some(note),
                WritePlan { replace: false, clear: &[] })?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Apply a per-record `tests` write (#166) — a MERGING, stamped write of just `tests`, so `bsc ui tests
/// set` can pair ONE record without a whole-tree `harvest` re-mirroring every other paired record (and
/// dragging along whatever a stale re-read of an UNRELATED record happened to hold — the `terminalhost`
/// `provides` loss #166 was filed against: a re-emitted record carried an explicit `null` for a field a
/// concurrent write had since given a real value, and `merge_over` honours an explicit `null` as
/// "remove this", #4197).
///
/// Exported for the same reason [`apply_relink`] is: the verb's file read lives in `bsc-ui` (a crate
/// above this one), while the write must still go through the same stamped path every other component
/// write uses — so a per-test pairing bumps `rev`, records attribution, and lands in `bsc ui log` like
/// any edit. `Err` when `id` names no existing record: this PAIRS a record, it does not create one.
/// UPSERT, not replace — request #221, which was SILENT DATA LOSS.
///
/// `merge_over` merges FIELDS, so writing `{ id, tests }` replaced the whole `tests` ARRAY: a record
/// already carrying one test could never gain a second. Measured on `tabstrip`, which carried a
/// 12,293-byte test whose `src/` file no longer exists — so the record was the ONLY copy of those
/// assertions, and `bsc ui tests set` overwrote it with a 1,513-byte entry at exit 0. `bsc graph tests
/// set`, the algorithms twin, appended correctly the whole time: the two halves of one surface disagreed
/// because they had two implementations of the same thing. They share one now
/// ([`bsc_record::upsert_test`]), and [`bsc_record::guard_no_test_loss`] refuses any write that would
/// still lose carried bytes.
pub fn apply_tests_set(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    id: &str,
    tests: serde_json::Value,
    by: Option<&str>,
    note: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let prior = current_record(store, id)?;
    if prior.is_null() {
        return Err(format!(
            "no component with id '{id}' — `tests set` pairs an EXISTING record, it does not create \
             one; check the id with `bsc ui get {id}`, or author the record first with `bsc ui set`"
        ));
    }
    let tests = match tests.as_array() {
        Some(entries) => {
            let mut merged = prior.get("tests").cloned();
            for entry in entries {
                merged = Some(bsc_record::upsert_test(merged.as_ref(), entry.clone()));
            }
            merged.unwrap_or_else(|| serde_json::json!([]))
        }
        // A non-array payload cannot be merged entry-wise, so it is written as sent — and the guard
        // below still refuses it if that loses anything, rather than the shape deciding the outcome.
        None => tests,
    };
    let written: Vec<&str> = tests
        .as_array()
        .map(|a| a.iter().filter_map(|t| t.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)).collect())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    bsc_record::guard_no_test_loss(id, prior.get("tests"), Some(&tests), &written)?;
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(by);
    set_stamped(
        store,
        &[serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "tests": tests })],
        None,
        &writer,
        "component",
        Some(note.unwrap_or("tests set: pair one record's colocated test")),
        WritePlan { replace: false, clear: &[] },
    )?;
    Ok(())
}

fn set_stamped(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    items: &[serde_json::Value],
    if_version: Option<i64>,
    writer: &str,
    noun: &str,
    note: Option<&str>,
    plan: WritePlan<'_>,
) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    if if_version.is_some() && items.len() != 1 {
        return Err(format!(
            "--if-version guards a single {noun} write, but stdin held {} records — send exactly one record when using optimistic concurrency",
            items.len()
        ));
    }
    let now = crate::record::now_iso();
    let mut ids = Vec::new();
    for item in items {
        let id = bsc_json_store::cli::id_of(item, noun)?;
        let prior = current_record(store, &id)?;
        // WHICH records this session may write (`a-worker-writes-only-its-own-feature`).
        //
        // Here rather than at the verb dispatch, because THIS is the funnel: `set` takes its records
        // from stdin, so the id is not in argv and a dispatch-level guard could not see it. Every
        // component write lands here, so a verb added later is confined without remembering to be.
        //
        // The PRIOR record's feature governs. A payload carrying `"feature": "mine"` against a
        // component owned by `core` is the move confinement exists to stop, and reading the submitted
        // value would wave it through — the record would simply change hands. A record that does not
        // exist yet is judged on what it claims, so a new one cannot slip in unowned.
        if bsc_cli_util::session_features().is_some() {
            // A missing record reads as `Value::Null`, whose `get` is None — so the fallback to the
            // SUBMITTED feature is the new-record case, expressed without a second existence check.
            let owner = prior
                .get("feature")
                .or_else(|| item.get("feature"))
                .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
                .unwrap_or_default()
                .to_string();
            bsc_cli_util::require_feature_write(&id, &owner)?;
        }
        let prior_rev = crate::record::read_rev(&prior);
        if let Some(n) = if_version {
            if prior_rev != n {
                return Err(format!(
                    "version conflict on {noun} '{id}': its current rev is {prior_rev}, not {n} — it changed since you read it. Re-read (`bsc ui log {id}`) and retry."
                ));
            }
        }
        // #4197: a `set` MERGES over the stored record, so a write that restates only `srcText` keeps the
        // kit, role, edges and provenance it never mentioned — the same semantics #4154 gave
        // `bsc graph impl set`. `--replace` opts back into the verbatim whole-record write the app bridge
        // and the seed reconcile need; only that path can still delete by omission, and it says so.
        let mut stamped =
            if plan.replace { item.clone() } else { crate::record::merge_over(&prior, item, plan.clear) };
        if let Some(msg) = destructive_write_warning(&id, noun, &prior, &stamped, plan.clear) {
            eprintln!("{msg}");
        }
        crate::record::stamp_with_history(&mut stamped, &prior, writer, &now, note);
        store.set(&id, &serde_json::to_string(&stamped).map_err(|e| format!("set: {e}"))?)?;
        bsc_util::emit_ui_activity(noun, &id);
        // #43: editing a COMPONENT invalidates the last preview render — clear any stale `render-error` so
        // `bsc ui doctor` doesn't keep reporting the pre-edit throw for source that just changed. Best-effort
        // (a diagnostic side-effect must never fail the write); a no-op unless this id currently has an error.
        if noun == "component" {
            let _ = crate::preview_errors::clear(&id);
        }
        ids.push(id);
    }
    Ok(ids)
}

/// `set [--by <tag>] [--note <text>] [--if-version <n>] [--clear a,b] [--replace] [--dir D] [--pretty]`
/// (#3164/#3568/#4197) — the STAMPING upsert for a collection. Parses the ui-write flags, reads the
/// record(s) from stdin, runs the domain batch `validate` (the component srcText gate / the kit-axis
/// nudge), then MERGES + stamps + upserts each via [`set_stamped`], which also appends a change-history
/// entry (`--note` is its summary; `bsc ui log <id>` reads the log). Prints the written id(s). Shared by
/// the component and kit collections (`open` + `validate` + `noun` differ). Already ui-scope gated in
/// [`run`]. See [`WritePlan`] for the merge/`--replace` split.
fn cmd_set(
    args: &[String],
    open: fn(&Option<String>) -> Result<bsc_json_store::Store, String>,
    validate: fn(&[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<(), String>,
    noun: &'static str,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut pretty, mut by, mut if_version, mut file, mut note) =
        (None::<String>, false, None::<String>, None::<i64>, None::<String>, None::<String>);
    let (mut replace, mut clear) = (false, Vec::<String>::new());
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            // #4197: the write MERGES, so a value can no longer be removed by omitting it — removal is
            // explicit. Mirrors `bsc graph impl set --clear` (#4154) so the two stores read the same.
            "--clear" => {
                let raw = it.next().ok_or("--clear needs a comma-separated field list, e.g. --clear folder,src")?;
                clear.extend(raw.split(',').map(str::trim).filter(|f| !f.is_empty()).map(str::to_string));
            }
            // #4197: opt back into the verbatim whole-record write — for the app bridge, `bsc ui import`,
            // and `reconcileSeed`'s seed-authoritative reset, which a merge would stop from converging.
            "--replace" => replace = true,
            // #3849: store a record the write-time gate would REFUSE — the deliberate spec-only escape.
            // Carried in a process-global rather than a parameter because `validate` is a shared `fn`
            // pointer used by every store's `cmd_set`; threading a flag through would change that
            // signature for stores that have no gate to bypass. One-shot CLI process, set once here,
            // read once in `validate_component_batch`.
            "--force" => FORCE_WRITE.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
            // #3373: read the payload from a BARE-NAMED file in $BSC_SCRATCH instead of stdin, so a
            // restricted session can author multi-line records at all (a heredoc cannot be allow-listed
            // — newlines are command separators). Resolution + the traversal defence live in bsc-cli-util.
            "--file" => file = it.next().cloned(),
            "--by" => by = it.next().cloned(),
            // #3568: a human-readable summary of WHY this write happened, recorded in the change history.
            "--note" => note = it.next().cloned(),
            "--if-version" => {
                let raw = it.next().ok_or("--if-version needs an integer revision (see `bsc ui log <id>`)")?;
                if_version = Some(
                    raw.parse::<i64>()
                        .map_err(|_| format!("--if-version '{raw}' is not an integer"))?,
                );
            }
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "unexpected argument '{other}' — `set` reads the record(s) from stdin, or from                      --file <name> in $BSC_SCRATCH"
                ))
            }
        }
    }
    // The two are contradictory: `--replace` writes the payload verbatim, so there is nothing left for
    // `--clear` to remove. Refusing beats silently honouring one of them.
    if replace && !clear.is_empty() {
        return Err(
            "--clear and --replace contradict each other: --replace writes the record VERBATIM (a field \
             absent from the payload is already gone), while --clear removes fields from a MERGE. Pick one."
                .to_string(),
        );
    }
    let items = read_set_items(noun, file.as_deref())?;
    let store = open(&dir)?;
    // VALIDATE WHAT WILL BE STORED, not what was typed (#3849's hole).
    //
    // A write has MERGED by default since #4197, so a payload carries only the fields being changed —
    // `{"id":"githubpage","srcText":"…"}` is the ordinary shape. Validating the raw payload therefore
    // judged a record by fields it never restated: `validate_component_batch` reads `role` to decide
    // whether the page gate applies, so EVERY partial write slipped past it and a `role: page` record
    // that cannot render could be stored by any of them — the exact thing #3849 exists to prevent. It
    // also emitted the preview-oracle warning at a page, which is the visible half of the same bug and
    // how this was noticed.
    //
    // Under `--replace` the payload IS the record, so there is nothing to merge and the raw items are
    // already what will be stored.
    let validated: Vec<serde_json::Value> = if replace {
        items.clone()
    } else {
        items
            .iter()
            .map(|item| {
                let id = item.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
                match store.get(id) {
                    Ok(Some(raw)) => serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&raw)
                        .map(|prior| crate::record::merge_over(&prior, item, &clear))
                        .unwrap_or_else(|_| item.clone()),
                    // Unknown id (a create) or an unreadable row — the payload is the whole record.
                    _ => item.clone(),
                }
            })
            .collect()
    };
    validate(&validated)?;
    // #3729: a component store is keyed by id ALONE — writing an id that already lives under a DIFFERENT
    // kit silently OVERWRITES it. Warn (never reject) so a promote-over-a-builtin clobber is visible.
    if noun == "component" {
        warn_cross_kit_collision(&store, &items);
        // Deliberately over `items`, not `validated`: this warns the AUTHOR about source they just
        // wrote, at the moment they can still choose differently. A partial write that never restates
        // `srcText` gets no warning — re-reporting an import the caller did not touch is noise, and
        // noise is what made 53 GraphHost findings unreadable.
        warn_unresolvable_imports(&store, &items);
    }
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(by.as_deref());
    let plan = WritePlan { replace, clear: &clear };
    let ids = set_stamped(&store, &items, if_version, &writer, noun, note.as_deref(), plan)?;
    let json = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&ids) } else { serde_json::to_string(&ids) };
    println!("{}", json.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// The cross-kit id-overwrite warnings for a `set` batch (#3729) — PURE so the decision is under test;
/// the CLI prints each to stderr via [`warn_cross_kit_collision`]. The component store is keyed by id
/// ALONE (not by `(kit, id)`), so writing `fleetpage` under kit `harvested` SILENTLY OVERWRITES a
/// `fleetpage` already stored under `base-studio-code` — that bit a designer promoting a harvested page
/// over a builtin of the same name (they believed the two coexisted). One message per colliding id.
fn cross_kit_collision_warnings(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, items: &[serde_json::Value]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for item in items {
        let (Some(id), Some(new_kit)) = (
            item.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str),
            item.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str),
        ) else {
            continue;
        };
        let prior = current_record(store, id).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null);
        let prior_kit = prior.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        if !prior_kit.is_empty() && prior_kit != new_kit {
            out.push(format!(
                "warning: component '{id}' already exists under kit '{prior_kit}' — this write (kit '{new_kit}') \
                 OVERWRITES it, because the store is keyed by id, NOT by (kit, id). Rename one of them if you \
                 meant to keep both, or ignore this if the re-home is intended."
            ));
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Print each [`cross_kit_collision_warnings`] message to stderr. Non-blocking (never rejects) — a
/// deliberate re-home is legitimate and the write still lands.
fn warn_cross_kit_collision(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, items: &[serde_json::Value]) {
    for w in cross_kit_collision_warnings(store, items) {
        eprintln!("{w}");
    }
}

/// Every `@/components/<id>` specifier `src` imports, in source order, deduped.
///
/// A deliberately narrow scan: only this ONE specifier shape is checked, because it is the only
/// internal form whose resolvability is decidable entirely inside the store. The preview also accepts
/// PLATFORM modules (`@/shared/ui/…`, `@/store`) — the declared boundary the bundler stubs — and those
/// are enumerated in TypeScript; duplicating that list here would create two copies to keep in sync,
/// and a stale copy would warn about imports that are perfectly fine.
fn component_specifiers(src: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for (i, _) in src.match_indices("@/components/") {
        // Bounded by the quote that opened the specifier — a specifier is a string literal, so the
        // closing quote is the terminator regardless of which quote style the author used.
        let rest = &src[i..];
        let end = rest.find(['"', '\'', '`']).unwrap_or(rest.len());
        let spec = rest[..end].trim_end();
        if spec.len() > "@/components/".len() && !out.iter().any(|s| s == spec) {
            out.push(spec.to_string());
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Which `@/components/…` specifiers in a `set` batch resolve to NOTHING (#73, designer request).
///
/// `bsc ui set` only syntax-checks `srcText`, so a write naming a component that publishes no such
/// specifier is accepted and the break surfaces two tool-calls later at `bsc navigate` time — after
/// which the usual recovery is to inline the widget and lose the composition. Five components were
/// reverted that way in one session.
///
/// Resolution mirrors the preview resolver (`componentPreview.ts`, `siblingIndex` + its internal-spec
/// gate): a specifier resolves when some record `provides` it EXACTLY, or when some record's `src`
/// minus extension equals the specifier's path. Anything else makes the importer unbuildable — the
/// build genuinely refuses rather than quietly substituting a stub.
///
/// WARNS, never rejects: 30 of the 94 `@/components/` imports already in the store resolve to nothing,
/// and a hard refusal would make those records unsaveable on their next edit. The point is to tell the
/// author at the moment they can still choose differently, not to relitigate what is already stored.
fn unresolvable_component_imports(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    items: &[serde_json::Value],
) -> Vec<String> {
    let published = published_specifiers(store, items);
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for item in items {
        let Some(id) = item.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) else { continue };
        let src = item.get("srcText").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        let missing: Vec<String> = component_specifiers(src)
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|s| !published.contains(s))
            .collect();
        if missing.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let list = missing.join(", ");
        let target = missing[0].trim_start_matches("@/components/");
        // The suggested command is the MERGE write (#4197) — `set` reads its record from stdin and has
        // no `--provides` flag, so the obvious-looking `bsc ui set <id> --provides <spec>` is rejected
        // twice over (unknown flag, unexpected positional). Naming a command that errors would make
        // this warning worse than silence, so the exact form here is covered by a test.
        out.push(format!(
            "warning: '{id}' imports {list} — no record publishes {}, so the preview will refuse to \
             build it (an unresolvable internal import is not stubbed). Fix by making the target \
             publish the specifier: echo '{{\"id\":\"{target}\",\"provides\":\"{}\"}}' | bsc ui set",
            if missing.len() == 1 { "that specifier" } else { "those specifiers" },
            missing[0],
        ));
    }
    out
}

/// The `@/components/…` specifiers the store resolves — every record's `provides`, plus the implied
/// specifier for a record whose `src` (minus extension) is itself a `components/<id>` path. `items` is
/// folded in so a batch that introduces BOTH the importer and its target validates as a unit rather
/// than warning about a specifier the same write is publishing.
fn published_specifiers(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    items: &[serde_json::Value],
) -> std::collections::HashSet<String> {
    let stored = store.list();
    let parsed = stored.iter().filter_map(|r| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(r).ok());
    let mut out = std::collections::HashSet::new();
    for rec in parsed.chain(items.iter().cloned()) {
        if let Some(p) = rec.get("provides").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
            let p = p.trim();
            if !p.is_empty() {
                out.insert(p.to_string());
            }
        }
        if let Some(s) = rec.get("src").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
            let base = s.trim().rsplit_once('.').map_or(s.trim(), |(stem, _)| stem);
            if base.starts_with("components/") {
                out.insert(format!("@/{base}"));
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

fn warn_unresolvable_imports(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, items: &[serde_json::Value]) {
    for w in unresolvable_component_imports(store, items) {
        eprintln!("{w}");
    }
}

/// A valid component NAME — a PascalCase identifier: an uppercase ASCII first char, then ASCII
/// alphanumerics. React cannot treat a lowercase name as a component, so the capital is a real rule, not a
/// style one; alphanumeric-only keeps the derived `--<name>-<token>` conventions and JSX tag clean.
fn is_component_name_ident(name: &str) -> bool {
    let mut chars = name.chars();
    matches!(chars.next(), Some(c) if c.is_ascii_uppercase()) && chars.all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric())
}

/// Replace WHOLE-IDENTIFIER occurrences of `old` with `new` in `text` — `old` must be bounded on both
/// sides by a non-identifier char (or the string edge), so renaming `Button` never rewrites `IconButton`
/// or `ButtonGroup`. Identifier chars are ASCII alphanumeric, `_`, and `$` (the JS identifier set).
/// Component names are ASCII, so matching on char boundaries is safe. Used to rewrite the renamed
/// component's own `srcText`/`source` identifier.
fn rename_ident(text: &str, old: &str, new: &str) -> String {
    if old.is_empty() {
        return text.to_string();
    }
    let is_ident = |c: char| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_' || c == '$';
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < text.len() {
        if text[i..].starts_with(old) {
            let before_ok = i == 0 || !text[..i].chars().next_back().is_some_and(is_ident);
            let after = i + old.len();
            let after_ok = after >= text.len() || !text[after..].chars().next().is_some_and(is_ident);
            if before_ok && after_ok {
                out.push_str(new);
                i = after;
                continue;
            }
        }
        let ch = text[i..].chars().next().expect("i is a char boundary");
        out.push(ch);
        i += ch.len_utf8();
    }
    out
}

/// `rename <id> <NewName> [--by <tag>] [--note <text>] [--dir D] [--pretty]` (#3576) — rename a component
/// in place. `id` is the STABLE store key (frozen at creation, never re-derived), so only the NAME moves:
/// the record's `name` + the identifier in its `srcText`/`source`, and — because the composition graph is
/// NAME-keyed (`model.ts`) — every sibling's `composes[]` + `rules[].use` that named it, swept across the
/// SAME kit only (kits never cross). Every touched record gets a change-history entry (#3568). Everything
/// keyed by id (store key, history, tokens, cross-graph URN) is untouched. A ui-scope MUTATION.
fn cmd_rename(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut pretty, mut by, mut note) = (None::<String>, false, None::<String>, None::<String>);
    let mut positionals: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            "--by" => by = it.next().cloned(),
            "--note" => note = it.next().cloned(),
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            positional => positionals.push(positional.to_string()),
        }
    }
    let id = positionals
        .first()
        .ok_or("usage: bsc ui rename <id> <NewName> [--by <tag>] [--note <text>]")?;
    let new_name = positionals
        .get(1)
        .ok_or("usage: bsc ui rename <id> <NewName> — the new PascalCase name is required")?;
    if !is_component_name_ident(new_name) {
        return Err(format!(
            "'{new_name}' is not a valid component name — a component is a PascalCase identifier ([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)"
        ));
    }

    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let target_raw = store.get(id)?.ok_or_else(|| {
        format!("no component '{id}' in the store — nothing to rename (ids are stable; see `bsc ui list`)")
    })?;
    let target: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&target_raw)
        .map_err(|e| format!("stored component '{id}' is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
    let old_name = target.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
    if old_name.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!("component '{id}' has no `name` to rename"));
    }
    if old_name == *new_name {
        return Err(format!("component '{id}' is already named '{new_name}' — nothing to do"));
    }
    let kit_id = target.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();

    let records: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();
    // Collision: `composes` resolves by NAME within a kit, so two same-named components in one kit make it
    // ambiguous. Refuse before writing anything.
    let collides = records.iter().any(|r| {
        r.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(kit_id.as_str())
            && r.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(new_name.as_str())
            && r.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) != Some(id.as_str())
    });
    if collides {
        return Err(format!(
            "kit '{kit_id}' already has a component named '{new_name}' — a rename would make `composes` ambiguous (it resolves by name within a kit). Pick another name."
        ));
    }

    let now = crate::record::now_iso();
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(by.as_deref());
    let default_note = format!("renamed {old_name} → {new_name}");
    let note_str = note.as_deref().map(str::trim).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).unwrap_or(&default_note);

    let mut updated: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for mut rec in records {
        // The sweep is bounded to the renamed component's OWN kit — kits never cross, so a same-named
        // component elsewhere is a different component and must NOT be touched.
        if rec.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) != Some(kit_id.as_str()) {
            continue;
        }
        let rid = match rec.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
            Some(s) if !s.is_empty() => s.to_string(),
            _ => continue,
        };
        let mut changed = false;

        if rid == *id {
            rec["name"] = serde_json::Value::from(new_name.as_str());
            changed = true;
            // Rewrite the identifier in the component's own source (usage snippet + any vendored module).
            for field in ["srcText", "source"] {
                if let Some(s) = rec.get(field).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
                    let rewritten = rename_ident(s, &old_name, new_name);
                    if rewritten != s {
                        rec[field] = serde_json::Value::from(rewritten);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        // Every record in the kit: rewrite composes[] + rules[].use references to the old name.
        if let Some(arr) = rec.get_mut("composes").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array_mut) {
            for e in arr.iter_mut() {
                if e.as_str() == Some(old_name.as_str()) {
                    *e = serde_json::Value::from(new_name.as_str());
                    changed = true;
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(rules) = rec.get_mut("rules").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array_mut) {
            for rule in rules.iter_mut() {
                if rule.get("use").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(old_name.as_str()) {
                    rule["use"] = serde_json::Value::from(new_name.as_str());
                    changed = true;
                }
            }
        }

        if changed {
            let prior = current_record(&store, &rid)?;
            crate::record::stamp_with_history(&mut rec, &prior, &writer, &now, Some(note_str));
            store.set(&rid, &serde_json::to_string(&rec).map_err(|e| format!("rename write: {e}"))?)?;
            bsc_util::emit_ui_activity("component", &rid);
            updated.push(rid);
        }
    }

    let references_updated = updated.iter().filter(|u| *u != id).count();
    let out = serde_json::json!({
        "id": id,
        "from": old_name,
        "to": new_name,
        "kit": kit_id,
        "updated": updated,
        "referencesUpdated": references_updated,
    });
    let text = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out) } else { serde_json::to_string(&out) };
    println!("{}", text.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// `merge <from-id> <into-id> [--by <tag>] [--note <text>] [--dir D] [--pretty]` (#3592) — fold the
/// component `from` INTO `into` (the survivor) and remove `from`. The ACT step of the optimize loop
/// (`dupes`/`similar` only propose). `into` stays authoritative; every same-kit `composes[]`/`rules[].use`
/// that named `from` is repointed to `into` (deduped; a self-reference the fold would create is dropped),
/// then `from` is deleted. Every repointed record gets a change-history entry (#3568). Scoped to the kit
/// (`composes` is name-keyed; a cross-kit merge is refused). A ui-scope MUTATION, gated in [`run`].
fn cmd_merge(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut pretty, mut by, mut note) = (None::<String>, false, None::<String>, None::<String>);
    let mut positionals: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            "--by" => by = it.next().cloned(),
            "--note" => note = it.next().cloned(),
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            positional => positionals.push(positional.to_string()),
        }
    }
    let from_id = positionals.first().ok_or("usage: bsc ui merge <from-id> <into-id> [--by <tag>] [--note <text>]")?;
    let into_id = positionals.get(1).ok_or("usage: bsc ui merge <from-id> <into-id> — the survivor id is required")?;
    if from_id == into_id {
        return Err(format!("cannot merge '{from_id}' into itself"));
    }

    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let load = |id: &str| -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
        let raw = store
            .get(id)?
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("no component '{id}' in the store (see `bsc ui list --raw`)"))?;
        serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("stored component '{id}' is not valid JSON: {e}"))
    };
    let from = load(from_id)?;
    let into = load(into_id)?;
    let from_name = from.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
    let into_name = into.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
    if from_name.is_empty() || into_name.is_empty() {
        return Err("both components must have a `name` to merge".to_string());
    }
    let from_kit = from.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
    let into_kit = into.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
    if from_kit != into_kit {
        return Err(format!(
            "'{from_id}' is in kit '{from_kit}' but '{into_id}' is in '{into_kit}' — `composes` is name-keyed WITHIN a kit, so a cross-kit merge is unsafe. Move one into the other's kit first, or merge within a kit."
        ));
    }
    let kit_id = from_kit.to_string();

    let now = crate::record::now_iso();
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(by.as_deref());
    let default_note = format!("merged {from_name} → {into_name}");
    let note_str = note.as_deref().map(str::trim).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).unwrap_or(&default_note);

    let records: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();
    let mut repointed: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for mut rec in records {
        // Only same-kit records reference `from` by name; and the `from` record itself is being removed.
        if rec.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) != Some(kit_id.as_str()) {
            continue;
        }
        let rid = match rec.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
            Some(s) if !s.is_empty() && s != from_id => s.to_string(),
            _ => continue,
        };
        let own_name = rec.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let mut changed = false;

        if let Some(arr) = rec.get_mut("composes").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array_mut) {
            let mut seen: std::collections::BTreeSet<String> = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
            let mut next: Vec<serde_json::Value> = Vec::with_capacity(arr.len());
            let mut any = false;
            for e in arr.iter() {
                let Some(orig) = e.as_str() else { continue };
                let mapped: &str = if orig == from_name.as_str() { into_name.as_str() } else { orig };
                if orig == from_name.as_str() {
                    any = true; // a from → into repoint
                }
                // Drop a self-reference the fold would create, and dedup (a component that composed BOTH
                // `from` AND `into` must not end up composing `into` twice).
                if mapped == own_name.as_str() || !seen.insert(mapped.to_string()) {
                    any = true;
                    continue;
                }
                next.push(serde_json::Value::from(mapped));
            }
            if any {
                *arr = next;
                changed = true;
            }
        }
        if let Some(rules) = rec.get_mut("rules").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array_mut) {
            for rule in rules.iter_mut() {
                if rule.get("use").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(from_name.as_str()) {
                    rule["use"] = serde_json::Value::from(into_name.as_str());
                    changed = true;
                }
            }
        }

        if changed {
            let prior = current_record(&store, &rid)?;
            crate::record::stamp_with_history(&mut rec, &prior, &writer, &now, Some(note_str));
            store.set(&rid, &serde_json::to_string(&rec).map_err(|e| format!("merge write: {e}"))?)?;
            bsc_util::emit_ui_activity("component", &rid);
            repointed.push(rid);
        }
    }

    // Retire the merged-away component LAST, once every reference is repointed. A packaged BUILTIN gets
    // a suppression tombstone rather than a bare delete, so the fold survives the next hydrate (#96) —
    // see `retire_component`.
    let from_builtin = from.get("builtin").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool) == Some(true);
    let retired = retire_component(&store, from_id, from_builtin, Some(into_id))?;
    bsc_util::emit_ui_activity("component", from_id);

    let out = merge_report(from_id, into_id, &kit_id, &repointed, retired);
    let text = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out) } else { serde_json::to_string(&out) };
    println!("{}", text.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// `regroup [--kit <id>] [--dir D] [--dry-run] [--pretty]` (#3579) — re-derive every stored component's
/// `group` as a nested `/`-delimited FOLDER PATH from its `src` ([`crate::group_from_src`]), so a kit
/// organizes like a completed project's folders (`shared/ui/controls`, `features/github`). Rewrites ONLY
/// the records whose derived group differs (each write stamped + logged via [`set_stamped`]); a record
/// with no usable `src` is left untouched. `--kit` scopes the pass to one kit; `--dry-run` reports the
/// moves without writing. Prints `{ scanned, changed: [{ id, from, to }], applied }`. A ui-scope
/// mutation, gated in [`run`].
/// A record's FOLDER, accepting the legacy key (#4107 slice B).
///
/// The store holds records written under `group`, and the component seed dir is skipped by
/// `ensure_seeded`, so there is no config-mirror pass to migrate them. Every READ therefore accepts
/// both names while every WRITE emits only `folder`: a record migrates the first time it is rewritten,
/// and `bsc ui refolder` does the whole store in one pass. Nothing needs migrating before this ships.
pub(crate) fn record_folder(rec: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<&str> {
    rec.get("folder")
        .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
}

fn cmd_refolder(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut kit, mut dry, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false, false);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--kit" => kit = it.next().cloned(),
            "--dry-run" => dry = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "unknown flag '{other}' — usage: bsc ui regroup [--kit <id>] [--dry-run] [--pretty]"
                ))
            }
        }
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let mut scanned = 0usize;
    let mut changed = Vec::new();
    let mut updated = Vec::new();
    // `Store::list()` yields each record's VERBATIM JSON (NOT its id) — parse each directly; the id is
    // the record's own `id` field (which `set_stamped` also keys the write off).
    for raw in store.list() {
        let mut rec: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&raw)
            .map_err(|e| format!("a stored component is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
        if let Some(k) = &kit {
            if rec.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) != Some(k.as_str()) {
                continue;
            }
        }
        scanned += 1;
        let src = rec.get("src").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        // The legacy key, read HERE and nowhere else. `record_folder` no longer knows it (#4107's alias
        // is gone), and this is the one place that still must: a migration verb is the last reader of
        // the name it is retiring.
        let legacy = rec.get("group").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).filter(|v| !v.is_empty())
            .map(str::to_string);
        let derived = crate::folder_from_src(src);
        // WHY THIS IS NOT JUST `let Some(new) = derived else { continue }`:
        //
        // `folder` derives from `src`, so a record with NO src was skipped outright — and every one of
        // the 19 components still on `group` at 2026-08-25 was srcless. The only verb that could finish
        // #4107 structurally could not touch the records that needed it, which is why the rename stalled
        // at 19 and the compatibility shim stayed load-bearing for a year. (4118 recorded exactly this
        // trap for the ALGORITHMS store — "refolder counts all 75 as srcless and skips every one" — and
        // nobody noticed it was equally true here.)
        //
        // A srcless record carrying `group` is migrated BY VALUE: its folder is curated (`app/console`,
        // `features/planner/fleet`) and no `src` could reproduce it, so carrying the value across is the
        // only correct move as well as the only possible one. Re-derivation stays what it always was for
        // a record that HAS src.
        let new_folder = match (derived, &legacy) {
            (Some(d), _) => d,                      // has src: re-derive, unchanged behaviour
            (None, Some(g)) => g.clone(),           // srcless + legacy key: carry the value across
            (None, None) => continue,               // nothing to derive and nothing to carry
        };
        let old = record_folder(&rec).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
        if old == new_folder && legacy.is_none() {
            continue;   // already correct AND already migrated off the legacy key
        }
        let id = rec.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
        changed.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "from": old, "to": new_folder }));
        rec["folder"] = serde_json::Value::String(new_folder);
        // Drop the legacy key so a rewritten record carries ONE name for its folder — otherwise a stale
        // `group` lingers beside the new `folder` and the two can drift.
        if let Some(o) = rec.as_object_mut() { o.remove("group"); }
        updated.push(rec);
    }
    let applied = if !dry && !updated.is_empty() {
        let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(None);
        // #4197: the write MERGES, so dropping the legacy `group` key above is no longer enough — a
        // merge would carry the stored one straight back. Name it as an explicit clear, which is also
        // what puts it in the record's history `dropped` instead of leaving the removal implicit.
        let clear = ["group".to_string()];
        let plan = WritePlan { replace: false, clear: &clear };
        set_stamped(&store, &updated, None, &writer, "component", Some("refolder: folder path from src"), plan)?;
        true
    } else {
        false
    };
    let report = serde_json::json!({ "scanned": scanned, "changed": changed, "applied": applied });
    let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) } else { serde_json::to_string(&report) };
    println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}


/// `bsc ui features [--kit <id>] [--apply] [--pretty]` — the FEATURE-axis backfill
/// (`epic-the-graphs-are-split-by-feature-over-a-core`), and the report of what it would do.
///
/// DRY BY DEFAULT, the inverse of `refolder`'s `--dry-run`. `refolder` re-derives a field it already
/// owns; this one INTRODUCES a field across the whole store on a mapping a human has to agree with
/// first, so the safe direction is opposite: you read the plan, then pass `--apply`.
///
/// It reports three groups, and the third is the point:
/// - `changed`  — records whose domain would be set (or corrected), with from/to.
/// - `byDomain` — the resulting per-domain counts, so the shape of the split is visible BEFORE it lands.
/// - `unmapped` — records the mapping cannot place, listed by id and never given a default.
///
/// The unmapped list is why this is not a sweep. 44 of 448 records are hollow — no folder, no `kitId`
/// and no `name` — and a backfill that quietly bucketed them would bury a data-quality problem inside a
/// migration and call it done. They surface here, every run, until someone decides what they are.
///
/// A record whose stored domain already matches is left alone, so re-running is a no-op.
fn cmd_features(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut kit, mut apply, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false, false);
    let mut seed_dir: Option<String> = None;
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--kit" => kit = it.next().cloned(),
            "--seed-dir" => seed_dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--apply" => apply = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "unknown flag '{other}' — usage: bsc ui features [--kit <id>] [--apply] [--pretty] \
                     (reports only unless --apply)"
                ))
            }
        }
    }
    // `--seed-dir <dir>` — backfill the PACKAGED SEED directly, deriving each record's feature from
    // its OWN folder rather than from the store's copy.
    //
    // WHY IT EXISTS. The normal path reads the store and syncs onward, and that covered 294 of 306
    // packaged components. The other 12 are records whose STORE copy is hollow — no folder, no kitId,
    // no name — while the seed file holds the real record, folder and all. That is the store-vs-seed
    // drift this repo has both ways, and it meant the ownership gate (which reads the seed, because a
    // rule that depends on whose machine ran it is not a rule) could never reach full coverage through
    // the store.
    //
    // Deriving from the seed's own folder needs no store at all, so a hollow store copy cannot hide a
    // record from the rule. Same never-overwrite contract as the store path: a feature already written
    // is a decision, not a starting point.
    if let Some(seed_dir) = &seed_dir {
        let root = std::path::Path::new(seed_dir);
        if !root.is_dir() {
            return Err(format!("not a directory: {seed_dir}"));
        }
        let (mut scanned, mut already) = (0usize, 0usize);
        let (mut changed, mut unmapped) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        let mut by_feature: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, usize> = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
        let mut stack = vec![root.to_path_buf()];
        while let Some(d) = stack.pop() {
            let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&d) else { continue };
            for e in entries.flatten() {
                let p = e.path();
                if p.is_dir() {
                    stack.push(p);
                    continue;
                }
                if p.extension().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) != Some("json") {
                    continue;
                }
                let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(&p) else { continue };
                let Ok(mut rec) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&text) else { continue };
                // A kit bundle has no top-level `id` and is not a record.
                let Some(id) = rec.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).map(str::to_owned) else { continue };
                scanned += 1;
                let old = rec.get("feature").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
                if !old.is_empty() {
                    already += 1;
                    *by_feature.entry(old).or_default() += 1;
                    continue;
                }
                // Fall back to deriving from `src` when the record carries no `folder`. Not a guess:
                // `folder` IS derived from `src` (`bsc ui regroup` re-derives it), so a record with a
                // src and no folder is one nobody has re-foldered — not one whose home is unknown.
                // Without this the last packaged component stayed unplaced for want of a cached value
                // the record already carries.
                let folder = record_folder(&rec)
                    .map(str::to_owned)
                    .or_else(|| rec.get("src").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).and_then(crate::folder_from_src))
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                let Some(new) = crate::feature_from_folder(&folder) else {
                    unmapped.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "folder": folder }));
                    continue;
                };
                *by_feature.entry(new.clone()).or_default() += 1;
                changed.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "folder": folder, "to": new }));
                if apply {
                    if let Some(o) = rec.as_object_mut() {
                        o.insert("feature".into(), serde_json::Value::String(new));
                    }
                    let out = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&rec).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
                    std::fs::write(&p, format!("{out}\n")).map_err(|e| format!("cannot write {}: {e}", p.display()))?;
                }
            }
        }
        let report = serde_json::json!({
            "seedDir": seed_dir, "scanned": scanned, "alreadyCorrect": already,
            "changed": changed, "unmapped": unmapped, "byFeature": by_feature, "applied": apply,
        });
        let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) } else { serde_json::to_string(&report) };
        println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        return Ok(());
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let (mut scanned, mut already) = (0usize, 0usize);
    let (mut changed, mut unmapped, mut updated) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    let mut by_feature: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, usize> = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    for raw in store.list() {
        let rec: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&raw)
            .map_err(|e| format!("a stored component is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
        if let Some(k) = &kit {
            if rec.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) != Some(k.as_str()) {
                continue;
            }
        }
        scanned += 1;
        let id = rec.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
        let folder = record_folder(&rec).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
        let old = rec.get("feature").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
        let Some(new) = crate::feature_from_folder(&folder) else {
            // Report the folder we could not place ALONGSIDE the id: "which records are unmapped" and
            // "what shapes is the mapping missing" are different questions and this answers both.
            unmapped.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "folder": folder }));
            if !old.is_empty() {
                *by_feature.entry(old).or_default() += 1;   // an already-set domain still counts
            }
            continue;
        };
        *by_feature.entry(new.clone()).or_default() += 1;
        // NEVER OVERWRITE a feature already set. The derivation is a starting point, not an
        // authority: a record deliberately placed by hand — `toggle` is `DeployToggle`, owned by
        // `core` because four other features compose it, while its FOLDER stays the planner tree it
        // was lifted from — must survive every later re-run. Without this the backfill silently undid
        // curation on each invocation, which is how it was found: a hand placement reverted one
        // command later.
        if !old.is_empty() {
            already += 1;
            continue;
        }
        if old == new {
            already += 1;
            continue;
        }
        changed.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "folder": folder, "from": old, "to": new }));
        // Submit ONLY {id, domain}, never the round-tripped record.
        //
        // The write MERGES, so the two are equivalent — right up until a stored field is `null`. A
        // resubmitted explicit `null` reads as a CLEAR, so round-tripping the whole record deletes
        // every null field it carries. Measured on the real store before this line existed: 448
        // records went in, 401 fields came out where 402 should have, and the missing one was
        // `terminalhost.provides` — a stored null, silently dropped by a backfill that was only
        // supposed to ADD a field.
        //
        // Sending just the delta makes that unreachable: a field this command never names is a field
        // it cannot lose.
        updated.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "feature": new }));
    }
    let applied = if apply && !updated.is_empty() {
        let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(None);
        let plan = WritePlan { replace: false, clear: &[] };
        set_stamped(&store, &updated, None, &writer, "component", Some("features: ownership axis from folder"), plan)?;
        true
    } else {
        false
    };
    let report = serde_json::json!({
        "scanned": scanned,
        "alreadyCorrect": already,
        "changed": changed,
        "unmapped": unmapped,
        "byFeature": by_feature,
        "applied": applied,
    });
    let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) } else { serde_json::to_string(&report) };
    println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}
/// `bsc ui export <dir> [--dir <store>] [--pretty]` (#3606) — dump the component store to a folder tree,
/// `<dir>/<group>/<id>.json`, so components-as-data round-trips: the seed half `bsc ui import` reads it back.
/// Files are written pretty (readable git diffs); `--pretty` also indents the stdout report.
fn cmd_export(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut out, mut dir, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if !other.starts_with("--") && out.is_none() => out = Some(other.to_string()),
            other => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}' — usage: bsc ui export <dir> [--dir <store>] [--pretty]")),
        }
    }
    let out = out.ok_or("usage: bsc ui export <dir> [--dir <store>] [--pretty]")?;
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let out_root = std::path::Path::new(&out);
    let mut ids = Vec::new();
    for raw in store.list() {
        let rec: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("a stored component is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
        let id = rec.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).ok_or("a stored component has no `id`")?;
        // `folder` is a `/`-delimited FOLDER PATH (#3579) → nest the file, so the tree mirrors the
        // project. Read through `record_folder` so a record still carrying the legacy `group` key
        // exports into the same tree rather than silently flattening to the root.
        let folder = record_folder(&rec).unwrap_or("");
        let mut path = out_root.to_path_buf();
        for seg in folder.split('/').filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {
            path.push(seg);
        }
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&path).map_err(|e| format!("cannot create {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        path.push(format!("{id}.json"));
        let text = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&rec).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        std::fs::write(&path, text).map_err(|e| format!("cannot write {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        ids.push(id.to_string());
    }
    let report = serde_json::json!({ "exported": ids.len(), "dir": out, "ids": ids });
    let s = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) } else { serde_json::to_string(&report) };
    println!("{}", s.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui import <dir> [--dir <store>] [--pretty]` (#3606) — load a folder tree of component records into
/// the store (the load half of components-as-data). Each `*.json` is UPSERT by its `id`; a KIT BUNDLE
/// (`{"components":[…]}`, e.g. react-ui.json) is exploded so every component in it imports.
/// `bsc ui parity <seed-dir>` — compare what the app RENDERS against what it SHIPS (#4246).
///
/// ## Why this exists
///
/// Three guards already watch the graph and none of them looks at the thing that renders:
///
/// ```text
/// graphParity.test.ts   globs data/components/app/**       -> the SEED
/// GraphComponent.tsx    useAppStore(s => s.components…)    -> the STORE
/// reconcileSeed         store <-> seed, but returns early for a record with no `builtin`
/// ```
///
/// So a record whose store copy has drifted from its seed renders source nothing has ever compared
/// against anything. Measured on this machine: 8 of 22 `role: page` records differ, `skillspage` by 9137
/// characters — and two of those eight drifted because a seed fix landed and the store never followed,
/// which is #4207 in miniature.
///
/// ## Why a CLI verb and not a test
///
/// The store is SQLite behind this binary; vitest cannot read it, which is precisely why the existing
/// guards are all seed-side. Putting the comparison where the store already lives is the only place it
/// can be honest. It reads the seed with the SAME folder walk `bsc ui import` uses, so the two verbs
/// cannot disagree about what "the seed" means.
///
/// ## Reporting, not gating, by default
///
/// Exits 0 unless `--strict`. A guard that lands red protects nothing — it just teaches everyone to
/// ignore it (`record-link-debt` is this repo's worked example: a red parity test sat unnoticed because
/// CI is disabled). `--strict` is for a caller that has adjudicated the known set and wants the next
/// drift to fail.
fn cmd_parity(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut inp, mut dir, mut pretty, mut strict, mut role) =
        (None::<String>, None::<String>, false, false, None::<String>);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            "--strict" => strict = true,
            // Scope to one role — `--role page` is the #4246 question, since a page record IS the page.
            "--role" => role = it.next().cloned(),
            other if !other.starts_with("--") && inp.is_none() => inp = Some(other.to_string()),
            other => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}' — usage: bsc ui parity <seed-dir> [--role <r>] [--strict] [--dir <store>] [--pretty]")),
        }
    }
    let inp = inp.ok_or("usage: bsc ui parity <seed-dir> [--role <r>] [--strict] [--dir <store>] [--pretty]")?;
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;

    let mut files = Vec::new();
    collect_json_files(std::path::Path::new(&inp), &mut files).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {inp}: {e}"))?;
    files.sort();

    let mut same = 0usize;
    let mut drift: Vec<serde_json::Value> = Vec::new();
    let mut missing: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for f in &files {
        let raw = std::fs::read_to_string(f).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {}: {e}", f.display()))?;
        let seed: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("{} is not valid JSON: {e}", f.display()))?;
        let Some(id) = seed.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) else { continue };
        if let Some(want) = role.as_deref() {
            if seed.get("role").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default() != want {
                continue;
            }
        }
        let Some(stored_raw) = store.get(id)? else {
            // In the seed, absent from the store — it has never been hydrated here. Reported separately
            // from drift: "not yet seeded" and "seeded then diverged" need different remedies.
            missing.push(id.to_string());
            continue;
        };
        let stored: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&stored_raw)
            .map_err(|e| format!("stored record '{id}' is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
        let s_txt = stored.get("srcText").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        let d_txt = seed.get("srcText").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        if s_txt == d_txt {
            same += 1;
            continue;
        }
        drift.push(serde_json::json!({
            "id": id,
            "role": seed.get("role").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default(),
            "store": s_txt.chars().count(),
            "seed": d_txt.chars().count(),
            // Signed, because the drift runs BOTH ways and "the store is stale" is the wrong summary:
            // a positive delta is the store holding source the seed has never had.
            "delta": s_txt.chars().count() as i64 - d_txt.chars().count() as i64,
            "builtin": stored.get("builtin").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(false),
            "stamped": stored.get("seedHash").is_some(),
        }));
    }

    let report = serde_json::json!({
        "seedDir": inp, "role": role, "same": same,
        "drift": drift.len(), "missingFromStore": missing.len(),
        "records": drift, "missing": missing,
    });
    let s = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) } else { serde_json::to_string(&report) };
    println!("{}", s.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    if strict && !drift.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!(
            "{} record(s) render source that differs from what ships — `bsc ui parity {inp} --pretty` names them",
            drift.len()
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn cmd_import(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut inp, mut dir, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if !other.starts_with("--") && inp.is_none() => inp = Some(other.to_string()),
            other => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}' — usage: bsc ui import <dir> [--dir <store>] [--pretty]")),
        }
    }
    let inp = inp.ok_or("usage: bsc ui import <dir> [--dir <store>] [--pretty]")?;
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let mut files = Vec::new();
    collect_json_files(std::path::Path::new(&inp), &mut files).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {inp}: {e}"))?;
    files.sort(); // deterministic import order (stable across platforms)
    let mut ids = Vec::new();
    for f in &files {
        let raw = std::fs::read_to_string(f).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {}: {e}", f.display()))?;
        let v: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("{} is not valid JSON: {e}", f.display()))?;
        // A kit bundle → import each of its components; anything else is a single record.
        let records: Vec<&serde_json::Value> = match v.get("components").and_then(|c| c.as_array()) {
            Some(arr) => arr.iter().collect(),
            None => vec![&v],
        };
        for rec in records {
            let id = rec
                .get("id")
                .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("a record in {} has no `id`", f.display()))?;
            store.set(id, &serde_json::to_string(rec).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?)?;
            bsc_util::emit_ui_activity("component", id); // Design Studio live-focus (#2525) re-hydrates
            ids.push(id.to_string());
        }
    }
    let report = serde_json::json!({ "imported": ids.len(), "dir": inp, "ids": ids });
    let s = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) } else { serde_json::to_string(&report) };
    println!("{}", s.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// The store's bookkeeping fields a packaged SEED never carries (#139, verified against all 73
/// `features/settings/cards/*.json` seeds): the change-history stamp (`history`/`rev`/`updatedAt`/
/// `updatedBy`, #3164), the reconcile fingerprint (`seedHash`), and the runtime-computed flags
/// (`builtin`/`used`/`usageAssessed`/`version`). `bsc ui export` dumps a record VERBATIM (by design —
/// it round-trips through `bsc ui import`), so its output carries every one of these and cannot be
/// dropped straight into `src-tauri/data/components/app/**`; `sync-seed` strips them before it writes.
///
/// #158 — the list was short by `usageAssessed` (stamped by `usage-scan --apply`, see its own doc
/// comment) and `version` (a store-only defaulted key), so a `sync-seed --apply` after either had run
/// wrote both into the seed file and `seedRoundTrip.test.ts`'s "carries only fields the projection
/// preserves" case failed on the very next `terminalview.json` sync.
const SEED_BOOKKEEPING_FIELDS: &[&str] =
    &["history", "rev", "updatedAt", "updatedBy", "builtin", "seedHash", "used", "usageAssessed", "version"];

/// `bsc ui sync-seed <id>… --seed-dir <dir> [--dir <store>] [--apply] [--pretty]` (#139) — the
/// store-to-seed sync `bsc ui parity` diagnoses (123 of 337 drifted, measured) and nothing could act on:
/// `export` dumps EVERY field, including store bookkeeping no seed file has ever carried, so its output
/// can't be dropped into the packaged tree. `sync-impl-seed.mjs` already solves this for algorithm
/// IMPLEMENTATIONS, one id at a time; this is that fix's counterpart for COMPONENTS, mounted on `bsc ui`
/// instead of left as a script per this repo's rule that a capability lives on the `bsc` surface.
///
/// Deliberately BY ID, never a sweep — `parity`'s `delta` is signed because drift runs BOTH ways, so a
/// mass re-stamp would as often overwrite real seed content with stale store content as the reverse. A
/// read-only DRY RUN by default (matching `sync-impl-seed.mjs`'s own default); `--apply` writes. A READ
/// of the store — no `ui` write scope required, since only the on-disk seed file changes (exactly like
/// `bsc ui export`, which also writes files under a read-only gate).
fn cmd_sync_seed(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut seed_dir, mut dir, mut apply, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false, false);
    let mut only: Option<String> = None;
    let mut ids: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--seed-dir" => seed_dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--apply" => apply = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            // `--only <field>` — write exactly ONE field onto the seed record, leaving the rest as the
            // seed has it. Without it this verb is whole-body, and store and seed drift BOTH ways (its
            // own help says so), so syncing a NEW facet across many records would drag that unrelated
            // drift along under cover of the change. The algorithms side needed the same flag for the
            // same reason when the `feature` axis landed.
            "--only" => only = it.next().cloned(),
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other => ids.push(other.to_string()),
        }
    }
    let usage = "usage: bsc ui sync-seed <id>… --seed-dir <dir> [--dir <store>] [--only <field>] [--apply] [--pretty]";
    let seed_dir = seed_dir.ok_or(usage)?;
    if ids.is_empty() {
        return Err(usage.into());
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;

    // Index the seed tree ONCE by id. A kit BUNDLE (`{"components":[…]}`, no top-level `id`) is skipped —
    // this fix targets the one-record-per-file layout `bsc ui export`/`import` already use.
    let mut files = Vec::new();
    collect_json_files(std::path::Path::new(&seed_dir), &mut files)
        .map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {seed_dir}: {e}"))?;
    let mut seed_by_id: std::collections::HashMap<String, std::path::PathBuf> = std::collections::HashMap::new();
    for f in &files {
        let Ok(raw) = std::fs::read_to_string(f) else { continue };
        let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&raw) else { continue };
        if let Some(id) = v.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
            seed_by_id.insert(id.to_string(), f.clone());
        }
    }

    let (mut synced, mut up_to_date, mut missing_from_store, mut missing_from_seed) =
        (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    for id in &ids {
        let Some(raw) = store.get(id)? else {
            missing_from_store.push(id.clone());
            continue;
        };
        let Some(path) = seed_by_id.get(id) else {
            // Mirrors `sync-impl-seed.mjs`'s own SKIP wording: a record with no seed file needs
            // PROMOTING (a new file), not syncing (an existing one).
            missing_from_seed.push(id.clone());
            continue;
        };
        let mut stored: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("stored record '{id}' is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
        let obj = stored.as_object_mut().ok_or_else(|| format!("stored record '{id}' is not a JSON object"))?;
        for field in SEED_BOOKKEEPING_FIELDS {
            obj.remove(*field);
        }
        let seed_raw = std::fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        let seed: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&seed_raw).map_err(|e| format!("{} is not valid JSON: {e}", path.display()))?;
        // ONE field onto the seed record: everything else stays exactly as the seed has it, so no
        // unrelated drift rides along with the facet being synced.
        let stored = match &only {
            None => stored,
            Some(field) => {
                let mut merged = seed.clone();
                match (merged.as_object_mut(), stored.get(field)) {
                    (Some(m), Some(v)) => { m.insert(field.clone(), v.clone()); }
                    (Some(m), None) => { m.remove(field); }
                    _ => {}
                }
                merged
            }
        };
        if seed == stored {
            up_to_date.push(id.clone());
            continue;
        }
        if apply {
            let text = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&stored).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            std::fs::write(path, format!("{text}\n")).map_err(|e| format!("cannot write {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        }
        synced.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "path": path.display().to_string() }));
    }

    let report = serde_json::json!({
        "seedDir": seed_dir, "applied": apply,
        "synced": synced, "upToDate": up_to_date,
        "missingFromStore": missing_from_store, "missingFromSeed": missing_from_seed,
    });
    let s = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) } else { serde_json::to_string(&report) };
    // Through the SHARED emitter (unlike `export`/`parity`/`import`'s plain `println!`) so a warm `bsc
    // serve` child can answer this read too, and so the report is capturable in tests.
    bsc_util::emit_line(&s.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui promote <id>… --seed-dir <dir> [--dir <store>] [--apply] [--pretty]` (#162, request from
/// kevin) — writes a genuinely NEW record's content into a NEW file under the packaged seed. `sync-seed`
/// deliberately declines exactly this case (its own report calls it out: "an id with no matching seed
/// file — that is a PROMOTION — a new file — not a sync"), so authoring a new component in the store had
/// no path to git — the request's evidence is a hand-written
/// `src-tauri/data/components/app/features/studio-sessions/networkarchitectmount.json`. `bsc graph
