            &store,
            &patches,
            None,
            "feature-rename",
            "component",
            Some(&format!("feature: {from} -> {to}")),
            WritePlan::default(),
        )?;
    }
    let out = serde_json::json!({
        "from": from, "to": to, "under": under, "applied": apply, "matched": matched.len(),
        // A SAMPLE — the point of a dry run is that a person reads it, and 154 ids is not read.
        "sample": matched.iter().take(8).filter_map(|v| v.get("id").cloned()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    });
    let json = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out) } else { serde_json::to_string(&out) };
    bsc_util::emit_line(&json.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// `doctor [--kit K] [--sound-kit id@version] [--json] [--pretty]` (#2678) — the graph-health report.
/// Reads the component store, runs the pure analyzer ([`crate::graph_health::analyze_with`]), and prints
/// the ranked findings as JSON (`--json`, LLM-consumable) or a human summary. `--kit` scopes the OUTPUT to
/// one kit (the analyzer always groups by kit, so edges never cross kits regardless).
///
/// `--sound-kit` (#3412) names the project's PINNED sound kit, so `@bsc/sounds/<id>` references are judged
/// against the kit the project actually adopted — the Rust twin of the Design Studio passing its resolved
/// `SoundKitSelection`. Omitted ⇒ the packaged default kit (an unpinned project, unchanged). A ref the
/// release store does not hold is a HARD ERROR, never a quiet fall back to the default: reporting a pinned
/// project against the starter kit would call broken references clean.
/// Read a PINNED sound kit's artifact out of the global versioned release store (#3412, `bsc sound
/// release`) — the same artifact the Design Studio resolves through the `bsc` bridge, so both sides judge
/// `@bsc/sounds/…` against identical bytes.
///
/// FAILS LOUDLY on a ref the store does not hold (or a malformed `id@version`) rather than degrading to
/// the packaged default: the caller asked for a specific kit, and answering with a different one would
/// report a component's broken sound references as clean. Mirrors the frontend's `unresolved` arm.
fn read_pinned_sound_kit(kit_ref: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let (id, version) = bsc_sound::release::split_ref(kit_ref)?;
    let store = bsc_sound::release::ReleaseStore::open_default()?;
    store
        .artifact(id, version)?
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("sound kit '{kit_ref}' is not in the sound-kit store (`bsc sound release list`)"))
}

/// `bsc ui backing <path>` / `bsc ui backing gate <path>...` (#4193).
///
/// The read answers "does this file have a record?"; the gate turns that into a refusal, so a change that
/// edited the artifact instead of the source cannot land quietly. Rejecting rather than warning is the
/// point: a warning at landing time becomes noise and is ignored, and the drift it was meant to stop
/// accumulates anyway.
fn cmd_backing(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut json, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, false, false);
    let mut positional: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--json" => json = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other => positional.push(other.to_string()),
        }
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let records: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();

    // #4223 — `audit` lists every record whose `src` names a file that is not here. That is the gate's
    // blind spot: it matches paths against `src`, so a stale pointer makes the record invisible and the
    // gate answers "not backed" for a file that IS backed.
    if positional.first().map(String::as_str) == Some("audit") {
        let root = std::env::current_dir().map_err(|e| format!("cannot resolve the current directory: {e}"))?;
        let bad = crate::backing::unresolvable_src(&records, &root);
        let payload = serde_json::json!({
            "root": root.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/"),
            "records": records.len(),
            "unresolvable": bad.len(),
            "stale": bad.iter()
                .map(|b| serde_json::json!({ "id": b.id, "kitId": b.kit_id, "src": b.src }))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        });
        bsc_cli_util::emit(pretty, json, &payload, || {
            if bad.is_empty() {
                return format!("ok: all {} record(s) name a `src` that exists here", records.len());
            }
            // GROUP BY KIT. A kit that describes a DIFFERENT project (a generated app, the react-d3
            // library) legitimately names paths this repo does not have, so a flat total mixes real
            // staleness with records that were never about this tree — and a number that cries wolf is
            // one people stop reading. The kit you are standing in is the one whose count means "stale".
            let mut by_kit: std::collections::BTreeMap<&str, Vec<&crate::backing::Backing>> = Default::default();
            for b in &bad {
                by_kit.entry(if b.kit_id.is_empty() { "(no kit)" } else { &b.kit_id }).or_default().push(b);
            }
            let mut out = format!(
                "{} of {} record(s) name a `src` that does not exist here, by kit:
",
                bad.len(),
                records.len()
            );
            for (kit, items) in &by_kit {
                out.push_str(&format!("
  {kit} — {} record(s)
", items.len()));
                for b in items.iter().take(12) {
                    out.push_str(&format!("    {:<32} {}
", b.id, b.src));
                }
                if items.len() > 12 {
                    out.push_str(&format!("    … and {} more
", items.len() - 12));
                }
            }
            out.push_str(
                "
A kit describing ANOTHER project names paths this repo does not have — that is expected. 
                 The gate is only blind where a kit meant to describe THIS tree points at a missing file.
",
            );
            out
        });
        return Ok(());
    }

    if positional.first().map(String::as_str) == Some("gate") {
        let paths = &positional[1..];
        if paths.is_empty() {
            return Err("usage: bsc ui backing gate <path>... — pass the files your change touches (e.g. `git diff --name-only`)".into());
        }
        let mut blocked = Vec::new();
        for p in paths {
            for b in crate::backing::backing_for(&records, p) {
                blocked.push(crate::backing::rejection(p, &b));
            }
        }
        // #4223: the verdict is only as good as the store's `src` pointers. Say so when some cannot be
        // resolved, on BOTH outcomes — a clean pass is exactly when a false negative does its damage.
        let root = std::env::current_dir().unwrap_or_default();
        let blind = crate::backing::unresolvable_src(&records, &root).len();
        if blind > 0 {
            eprintln!("{}", crate::backing::blind_spot_caveat(blind));
        }
        if blocked.is_empty() {
            // Say so explicitly: a silent pass is indistinguishable from a gate that did not run.
            println!("ok: none of the {} path(s) is component-backed", paths.len());
            return Ok(());
        }
        return Err(blocked.join("

"));
    }

    let path = positional
        .first()
        .ok_or("usage: bsc ui backing <path> | bsc ui backing gate <path>...")?;
    let found = crate::backing::backing_for(&records, path);
    let payload = serde_json::json!({
        "path": crate::backing::normalize(path),
        "backed": !found.is_empty(),
        "records": found.iter()
            .map(|b| serde_json::json!({ "id": b.id, "kitId": b.kit_id, "src": b.src }))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    });
    bsc_cli_util::emit(pretty, json, &payload, || {
        if found.is_empty() {
            format!("{} — not component-backed", crate::backing::normalize(path))
        } else {
            found.iter()
                .map(|b| format!("{} — component `{}` (kit `{}`)", crate::backing::normalize(path), b.id, b.kit_id))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join("
")
        }
    });
    Ok(())
}

/// `library get <name-or-spec> [--pretty]` (bsc request #118) — verify a `doctor`
/// `@bsc/algorithms/<name>` LIBRARY-reference finding without the `bsc graph` grant the Design Studio's
/// designer session never carries. A pure read over [`crate::graph_health::resolve_algorithm_library_node`],
/// the SAME resolution `doctor`'s `reimplementation`/`unresolvable-import` findings judge a component
/// against, so this verb's answer and doctor's finding can never disagree.
fn cmd_library(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    match args.first().map(String::as_str) {
        Some("get") => {}
        Some(other) => return Err(format!("unknown `library` command '{other}' — try: get")),
        None => return Err("usage: bsc ui library get <name-or-spec> [--pretty]".to_string()),
    }
    let (mut pretty, mut name) = (false, None::<&str>);
    for a in &args[1..] {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other if name.is_none() => name = Some(other),
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    let name = name.ok_or("usage: bsc ui library get <name-or-spec> [--pretty]")?;
    let payload = match crate::graph_health::resolve_algorithm_library_node(name) {
        crate::graph_health::LibraryLookup::Found(im) => {
            let mut obj = im;
            if let Some(map) = obj.as_object_mut() {
                map.insert("resolves".to_string(), serde_json::Value::Bool(true));
            }
            obj
        }
        crate::graph_health::LibraryLookup::NotFound => {
            serde_json::json!({ "resolves": false, "queried": name })
        }
        // A bare NAME naming several typescript algorithms is refused rather than guessed — the same
        // call `bsc graph impl get` makes, and for the same reason (#118): a wrong silent pick on a
        // verification read is worse than the miss `resolves: false` already covers as a normal answer.
        crate::graph_health::LibraryLookup::Ambiguous(ids) => {
            return Err(format!(
                "'{name}' names {} implementations — pass the exact id instead (e.g. `@bsc/algorithms/{}`): {}",
                ids.len(),
                ids.first().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or(name),
                ids.join(", ")
            ));
        }
    };
    let json = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&payload) } else { serde_json::to_string(&payload) };
    // Through the SHARED emitter, not `println!` — byte-identical when nothing is capturing, but it
    // lets a warm `bsc serve` child answer this READ off the same stdout it speaks its protocol on
    // (see `cmd_scan_cache`'s `get` arm, the other JSON read that already does this).
    bsc_util::emit_line(&json.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// Map the runtime lens (`bsc_runtime::doctor`) onto this doctor's `Finding` shape.
///
/// The ANALYSIS lives in `bsc-runtime`, beside the data, so `bsc graph doctor` asks the same question of
/// the same rows rather than growing a second answer that drifts. Only the presentation is here.
///
/// `src_hash` is computed from each record's CURRENT `srcText` with the same function the frontend uses
/// when it records what it compiled — that equality is the whole basis of the `stale` finding, and it is
/// pinned across the language boundary by `data/runtime/hash.fixtures.json`.
///
/// A missing/unreadable runtime.db is NOT an error: it means the app has not run with attestation on,
/// which is a normal state on a fresh checkout, and failing the whole health report over it would make
/// `--runtime` unusable exactly when someone first reaches for it.
fn runtime_findings(comps: &[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<Vec<crate::graph_health::Finding>, String> {
    let Some(path) = bsc_runtime::default_db_path() else {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    };
    let Ok(store) = bsc_runtime::Store::open(&path) else {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    };
    let rows = store.list(&bsc_runtime::Filter::default()).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

    let text = |v: &serde_json::Value, k: &str| {
        v.get(k).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string()
    };
    let records: Vec<bsc_runtime::doctor::RecordRef> = comps
        .iter()
        .map(|c| bsc_runtime::doctor::RecordRef {
            id: text(c, "id"),
            src_hash: {
                let src = text(c, "srcText");
                if src.is_empty() { String::new() } else { bsc_runtime::src_hash(&src) }
            },
        })
        .collect();
    // Name → id, so a finding reads as the component rather than as a slug.
    let name_of = |id: &str| -> String {
        comps
            .iter()
            .find(|c| text(c, "id") == id)
            .map(|c| {
                let n = text(c, "name");
                if n.is_empty() { id.to_string() } else { n }
            })
            .unwrap_or_else(|| id.to_string())
    };
    let kit_of = |id: &str| -> String {
        comps.iter().find(|c| text(c, "id") == id).map(|c| text(c, "kitId")).unwrap_or_default()
    };

    let report = bsc_runtime::doctor::analyze(&rows, &records);
    if report.unmeasured {
        // ONE finding, not hundreds. "Nothing has served" is true and useless here; what the reader needs
        // is to know the lens has no data, which is a different statement entirely.
        return Ok(vec![crate::graph_health::Finding {
            category: "runtime-unmeasured",
            severity: 1,
            kit: String::new(),
            node_ids: Vec::new(),
            node_names: Vec::new(),
            why: "runtime.db holds no attestations — the app has not run with attestation on, so NO \
                  runtime judgement is available (this is not the same as 'nothing ran')"
                .into(),
            suggested_action: "start the app, use the surfaces you care about, then re-run; `bsc runtime summary` shows what has been measured".into(),
        }]);
    }
    Ok(report
        .findings
        .into_iter()
        .map(|f| crate::graph_health::Finding {
            category: runtime_category(f.category),
            severity: f.severity,
            kit: kit_of(&f.record_id),
            node_names: vec![name_of(&f.record_id)],
            node_ids: vec![f.record_id],
            why: f.why,
            suggested_action: f.suggested_action,
        })
        .collect())
}

/// Map a runtime finding's category onto a `&'static str` this doctor's `Finding` requires. Explicit
/// rather than leaked: the categories are a closed set, and an unknown one should read as unknown rather
/// than being silently dropped or leaking a runtime-owned string into a report shape it does not own.
fn runtime_category(c: &str) -> &'static str {
    match c {
        "declined" => "runtime-declined",
        "fell-back" => "runtime-fell-back",
        "render-threw" => "runtime-render-threw",
        "stale" => "runtime-stale",
        "never-ran" => "runtime-never-ran",
        "recompile-loop" => "runtime-recompile-loop",
        "slow-compile" => "runtime-slow-compile",
        _ => "runtime-unknown",
    }
}

/// #114: split a `--category` argument into normalized names — comma-separated, trimmed, empty
/// segments dropped so a stray trailing comma or extra space doesn't quietly produce an unmatchable
/// empty-string category. Pure, so the parsing is unit-testable without a store or the printed report.
fn parse_category_arg(raw: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    raw.split(',').map(str::trim).filter(|c| !c.is_empty()).map(str::to_string).collect()
}

fn cmd_doctor(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut kit, mut json, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false, false);
    let (mut fix, mut yes, mut motion) = (false, false, false);
    let mut runtime = false;
    let mut imports = false;
    let mut sound_kit = None::<String>;
    // #114: isolate one (or a few) categories out of a 200+ finding report without a helper script.
    // Comma-separated, same convention as the `set --clear` list flag elsewhere in this CLI.
    let mut category: Option<Vec<String>> = None;
    let mut repo = None::<String>;
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--kit" => kit = it.next().cloned(),
            // #3412: resolve `@bsc/sounds/…` against the project's PINNED kit instead of the packaged default.
            "--sound-kit" => sound_kit = it.next().cloned(),
            // #3888/`bsc request` #95: where the app's REAL entry point lives, for the host-mount +
            // `provides` reachability walk (`usage_sources::reachable_ids`) that populates `used` for
            // findings — else the cwd (a doctor run is normally from the repo whose kit it's reporting on).
            "--repo" => repo = it.next().cloned(),
            "--json" => json = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            "--fix" => fix = true,
            "--yes" => yes = true,
            // #3163: ADD the four mechanical MOTION checks to the report (an animation selector whose class
            // hook the source never renders · a stroke-dash keyframe with no pathLength · a CSS transform
            // keyframe fighting an SVG transform= attribute · a cross-component keyframe-name collision).
            "--motion" => motion = true,
            // #doctor-reads-the-runtime: ADD the findings the structural pass structurally cannot see —
            // what the app OBSERVED while running (declined / never-ran / stale / fell-back /
            // recompile-loop / slow-compile), read from runtime.db.
            "--runtime" => runtime = true,
            // #149: ADD the record-CLOSURE symbol check — walks each record's `@/…` imports through
            // `unresolvable-import`'s SAME resolution chain (sibling → component `provides` → impl
            // `provides`, barrels followed) and reports a name the target resolves to but never exports.
            "--imports" => imports = true,
            // #114: filter the report to one or more categories (comma-separated), e.g.
            // `--category dangling-branch` or `--category dangling-branch,orphan`.
            "--category" => {
                let raw = it.next().ok_or("--category needs a value")?;
                category = Some(parse_category_arg(raw));
            }
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    // The write path (`--fix --yes`) removes records, so honor the runtime `ui` write-scope (#2470) —
    // a read-scoped session may run the report but not prune. A dry run stays read-only.
    if fix && yes {
        bsc_cli_util::require_write_scope("ui")?;
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    // UNFILTERED — a `--kit`-scoped report still needs the FULL store + impls to resolve a
    // cross-kit `provides` import or an algorithm-impl hop correctly (#3888); only the FINDINGS below
    // are kit-scoped, never the usage corpus.
    let all_comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();
    let repo_path = repo.map(std::path::PathBuf::from).or_else(|| std::env::current_dir().ok());
    let usage = crate::usage_sources::reachable_ids(
        &all_comps,
        &bsc_graph::implementations(),
        crate::graph_health::platform_modules(),
        repo_path.as_deref(),
    );
    let kit_filter = |v: &&serde_json::Value| match &kit {
        Some(k) => v.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(k.as_str()),
        None => true,
    };
    // The store's real, PERSISTED `used` — never touched by the enrichment below. `prune_plan_with`'s
    // guard is judged against this, not `comps`, so `--fix --yes`'s deletion eligibility is completely
    // unaffected by this run's ephemeral reachability walk (see `prune_plan_with`'s doc for why).
    let comps_disk_truth: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        all_comps.iter().filter(kit_filter).cloned().collect();
    let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> = crate::usage_sources::enrich_used(&all_comps, &usage.reached)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|v| kit_filter(&v))
        .collect();

    if fix {
        return doctor_fix(&store, &comps, &comps_disk_truth, yes);
    }

    // Resolve the pin BEFORE analyzing so a broken pin fails the whole report rather than silently
    // producing one measured against the wrong kit (#3412).
    let sound_kit_json = match &sound_kit {
        Some(kit_ref) => Some(read_pinned_sound_kit(kit_ref)?),
        None => None,
    };
    let opts = crate::graph_health::HealthOptions { sound_kit_json: sound_kit_json.as_deref() };
    let mut findings = crate::graph_health::analyze_with(&comps, &opts);
    // A `provides` COLLISION is a correctness defect, not a tidiness suggestion: `provides` is a global
    // override, so the loader resolves the specifier to ONE record and every other claimant is a dead
    // override that still reads as live — decided by store iteration order.
    //
    // The detection (#4138) was reachable only from `dupes`, the propose-only dedup surface. `doctor` is
    // the report people run as a health check, and it returned 560 findings across 14 categories without
    // mentioning four live collisions. Reported in BOTH places now; `dupes` keeps it because that is
    // where the keeper recommendation belongs.
    findings.extend(crate::similarity::provides_collision_findings(&comps));
    // #129: the mirror case — records that disagree about a shared `src_path`'s specifier rather than
    // colliding on one. Same rationale for appearing in both `dupes` and `doctor` as the collision
    // finding above: `dupes` is the propose-a-merge surface, `doctor` is the health check people run.
    findings.extend(crate::similarity::provides_split_findings(&comps));
    if motion {
        // #3163: append the motion findings (re-ranked with the render errors below).
        findings.extend(crate::graph_health::analyze_motion(&comps));
    }
    // #3540: append the RENDER errors — the runtime throws doctor's static analysis can't see, read from
    // the durable preview-error log the app's scan + previews record. Scoped to `comps` (already
    // kit-filtered), so `--kit` narrows these too. Always on: a preview that throws is the most
    // actionable finding, so it should never need a flag to surface.
    let render_errors = crate::preview_errors::latest_error_by_id();
    findings.extend(crate::graph_health::render_error_findings(&comps, &render_errors));
    // #a-composes-target-can-name-two-records: append the NAME COLLISIONS — two records in one kit
    // answering to one name, so a `composes` entry naming it resolves to whichever comes first in store
    // order. Appended here rather than added to `analyze_with` because that function has a BYTE-PARITY
    // TS twin (`graphHealth.ts`); this is the same reason `analyze_motion` and the render errors live
    // out here. Always on: nothing else in the tooling can report the property (`dupes` found 6 of 39
    // on the live library, because it detects content similarity and these records collide while
    // DIFFERING in content).
    findings.extend(crate::graph_health::analyze_name_collisions(&comps));
    // #3544: append the library-wide NEAR-duplicate findings — the fuzzy layer (name + contract distance)
    // the exact per-kit `duplicate` detector misses (`Donut`≈`DonutChart`, cross-kit `Card` repeats).
    // PROPOSE-ONLY: emitted here, never fed to `--fix` (only byte-identical merges auto-apply). Cross-kit
    // by nature, so it fires on the full report; a `--kit` scope filters `comps`, leaving within-kit dups.
    findings.extend(crate::similarity::near_duplicate_findings(&comps, crate::similarity::DEFAULT_THRESHOLD));
    // #doctor-reads-the-runtime: the RUNTIME lens. Behind a flag, unlike the render errors above, because
    // it answers a different KIND of question and its most useful finding — DECLINED — depends on the app
    // having run. A store with no attestations says so once rather than calling every record dead.
    if runtime {
        findings.extend(runtime_findings(&comps)?);
    }
    // #149: the record-CLOSURE symbol lens. Behind a flag like `--runtime`/`--motion` — it needs the
    // WHOLE algorithms store (`bsc_graph::implementations()`) to resolve a `provides` target, a real
    // read `analyze_with`'s pure per-kit pass never makes, and it is a different KIND of question from
    // module-level `unresolvable-import`: does the specifier resolve to something that names THIS symbol.
    if imports {
        let impls = bsc_graph::implementations();
        let platform = crate::graph_health::platform_modules();
        let index = crate::closure::Index::new(&comps, &impls, platform, None);
        let mut records: Vec<(String, String, String, String)> = comps
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|c| {
                let id = c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)?.to_string();
                let src = c.get("srcText").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
                if src.trim().is_empty() {
                    return None;
                }
                let kit = c.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
                let name = c.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or(&id).to_string();
                Some((kit, id, name, src.to_string()))
            })
            .collect();
        records.extend(impls.iter().filter_map(|im| {
            let id = im.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)?.to_string();
            let src = im.get("code").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
            if src.trim().is_empty() {
                return None;
            }
            let name = im.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or(&id).to_string();
            Some((String::new(), id, name, src.to_string()))
        }));
        findings.extend(crate::import_symbols::unresolved_import_symbol_findings(&records, &index));
    }
    // #114: narrow to the requested categories AFTER every lens has contributed, so `--category` composes
    // with `--motion`/`--runtime` instead of pre-empting them.
    if let Some(wanted) = &category {
        findings.retain(|f| wanted.iter().any(|c| c == f.category));
    }
    // Re-rank the combined report (most-severe first, stable kit + node-name tiebreak — the SAME ordering
    // `analyze` uses). Render errors (severity 5) sort to the top.
    findings.sort_by(|a, b| {
        b.severity
            .cmp(&a.severity)
            .then_with(|| a.kit.cmp(&b.kit))
            .then_with(|| a.node_names.first().cmp(&b.node_names.first()))
    });

    if json {
        let arr: Vec<serde_json::Value> = findings.iter().map(crate::graph_health::Finding::to_value).collect();
        let out = if pretty {
            serde_json::to_string_pretty(&arr)
        } else {
            serde_json::to_string(&arr)
        };
        println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        return Ok(());
    }

    // The usage-source corpus, so it's INSPECTABLE rather than a black box (#3888) — a report from a
    // tree with no `src/app/main.tsx` (a different kit's context) says so, rather than silently reading
    // as "usage was checked and found none".
    if usage.entry_files_read == 0 {
        println!(
            "  (usage sources: no app entry point found under {} — host-mount/`provides` reachability was not checked; pass --repo)",
            repo_path.as_deref().map(|p| p.display().to_string()).unwrap_or_else(|| "<cwd>".to_string())
        );
    } else {
        println!(
            "  (usage sources: {} entry file(s), {} real file(s) scanned, {} record(s)/impl(s) proven reachable)",
            usage.entry_files_read,
            usage.files_scanned,
            usage.reached.len()
        );
    }

    // Human summary — one line per finding, most-severe first.
    if findings.is_empty() {
        let scope = kit.as_deref().map(|k| format!(" for kit '{k}'")).unwrap_or_default();
        match &category {
            // A category filter narrowing to zero is "clean for that category", not "clean overall" —
            // say so explicitly rather than reusing the whole-report health claim.
            Some(wanted) => println!("✓ no {} finding(s){scope}.", wanted.join(", ")),
            None => println!("✓ design graph is healthy{scope} — no orphans, dead branches, duplicates, cycles, unbuildable, or self-referential components."),
        }
        return Ok(());
    }
    println!("{} finding(s), most-severe first:", findings.len());
    for f in &findings {
        println!("  [{}] {} — {}", f.category, f.kit, f.why);
        println!("        → {}", f.suggested_action);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui dupes` (#3544) — the whole-library duplicate report: the exact `duplicate` findings the per-kit
/// analyzer emits (shared `wraps` / byte-identical source) PLUS the fuzzy NEAR-duplicates it misses (name +
/// contract distance — `Donut`≈`DonutChart`, cross-kit `Card` repeats), ranked together. The LLM-native
/// "what should I merge?" surface; PROPOSE-ONLY — the proposals guide a manual/designer merge, there is no
/// `--fix` here. `--kit` scopes to one kit (dropping cross-kit near-dups); `--threshold <0..1>` tunes the
/// fuzzy bar (default [`crate::similarity::DEFAULT_THRESHOLD`]).
fn cmd_dupes(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut kit, mut json, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false, false);
    let mut explain = false;
    let mut threshold = crate::similarity::DEFAULT_THRESHOLD;
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--kit" => kit = it.next().cloned(),
            "--threshold" => {
                threshold = it
                    .next()
                    .and_then(|s| s.parse::<f64>().ok())
                    .ok_or("--threshold needs a number in [0,1]")?;
            }
            "--explain" => explain = true,
            "--json" => json = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> = store
        .list()
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok())
        .filter(|v| match &kit {
            Some(k) => v.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(k.as_str()),
            None => true,
        })
        .collect();
    // Conflicts first (#4138 — a `provides` collision has a definite answer), then exact duplicates
    // (certain — shared wraps / byte-identical), then the ranked near-duplicates.
    let mut findings: Vec<crate::graph_health::Finding> = crate::similarity::provides_collision_findings(&comps);
    findings.extend(crate::similarity::provides_split_findings(&comps));
    findings.extend(
        crate::graph_health::analyze(&comps).into_iter().filter(|f| f.category == "duplicate"),
    );
    findings.extend(crate::similarity::near_duplicate_findings(&comps, threshold));
    if json {
        let arr: Vec<serde_json::Value> = findings.iter().map(crate::graph_health::Finding::to_value).collect();
        let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&arr) } else { serde_json::to_string(&arr) };
        println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        return Ok(());
    }
    if findings.is_empty() {
        println!("✓ no duplicates or near-duplicates found.");
        return Ok(());
    }
    println!("{} duplicate / near-duplicate finding(s), most-similar first:", findings.len());
    let by_id: std::collections::BTreeMap<&str, &serde_json::Value> = comps
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|c| c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).map(|id| (id, c)))
        .collect();
    for f in &findings {
        println!("  [{}] {} — {}", f.category, f.kit, f.why);
        println!("        → {}", f.suggested_action);
        // #4138: WHY it ranked, not just that it did. Only a two-record finding has a pair to explain;
        // a `provides` collision spanning three is a conflict, not a scored pair.
        if !explain || f.node_ids.len() != 2 {
            continue;
        }
        let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (by_id.get(f.node_ids[0].as_str()), by_id.get(f.node_ids[1].as_str())) else {
            continue;
        };
        let Some(terms) = crate::similarity::explain_pair(a, b) else { continue };
        let (mut scored, mut dropped) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        for t in &terms {
            match t.value {
                // A term with no signal on EITHER side is DROPPED, not scored 0 — naming them is half
                // the point of the explanation, since an absent signal reads as disagreement otherwise.
                None => dropped.push(t.label),
                Some(v) => scored.push(format!("{}={v:.2}×{:.2}→{:.3}", t.label, t.weight, t.contribution())),
            }
        }
        println!("        · terms: {}", scored.join("  "));
        if !dropped.is_empty() {
            println!("        · no signal (dropped): {}", dropped.join(", "));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui similar <id> [--top N] [--threshold F]` (#3544) — the components most similar to <id> across the
/// WHOLE library (name + contract distance), ranked most-similar first. The discover-before-authoring read:
/// a session checks whether a component like the one it is about to build already exists. Cross-kit;
/// PROPOSE-ONLY. `--top` caps the rows (default 10); `--threshold` sets a minimum overall score.
/// The bar `bsc ui patterns` clusters at. MEASURED against the real library, and by a criterion rather
/// than by taste: **0.90 is the loosest bar at which no cluster is a CHAIN.**
///
/// | threshold | clusters | records | largest | cohesion 1.00 | chained |
/// |---|---|---|---|---|---|
/// | 1.00 | 14 | 40 | 5 | 14 | 0 |
/// | **0.90** | **16** | **45** | **5** | **13** | **0** |
/// | 0.85 | 19 | 53 | 5 | 13 | **2** |
/// | 0.80 | 19 | 59 | 5 | 10 | 3 |
/// | 0.70 | 22 | 83 | 11 | 7 | 5 |
/// | 0.60 | 35 | 135 | 24 | 5 | 6 |
///
/// Below 0.90 connected components start chaining — `A~B` and `B~C` grouping records that are not
/// themselves alike — and by 0.60 the largest "pattern" is a 24-member blob. Above it the extra
/// tightness costs two real clusters and buys nothing, since 0.95 and 1.00 return the same 14.
///
/// Re-measure before moving it; the value is only defensible against the distribution, exactly as
/// `MULTI_COMPONENT_MIN` and `FAMILY_SHELL_SHARE` are. Chained clusters are still REPORTED at any
/// threshold rather than dropped — `cohesion` is on every row — so a lower bar is a legible trade and
/// not a silent one.
const PATTERN_THRESHOLD: f64 = 0.90;

fn cmd_similar(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut json, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, false, false);
    let (mut id, mut top, mut floor) = (None::<String>, 10usize, 0.0f64);
    // #90: rank on STRUCTURE alone — the composes signature + the JSX skeleton — instead of name+contract.
    let mut shape = false;
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--top" => {
                top = it.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<usize>().ok()).ok_or("--top needs a positive integer")?;
            }
            "--threshold" => {
                floor = it.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<f64>().ok()).ok_or("--threshold needs a number in [0,1]")?;
            }
            "--shape" => shape = true,
            "--json" => json = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other if id.is_none() => id = Some(other.to_string()),
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui similar <id> [--shape] [--top N] [--threshold F]")?;
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();
    let Some(target) = comps.iter().find(|c| c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(id.as_str()))
    else {
        return Err(format!("no component with id '{id}' (see `bsc ui list --raw`)"));
    };
    // Ranking a TOMBSTONE is a fair question — "what is like the thing I retired?" — and it is answered
    // against the live library. But an empty or thin result here would otherwise be indistinguishable
    // from "nothing resembles it", when the real reason is that the record has no content left to score,
    // so say which one it is. (Tombstones are excluded as CANDIDATES throughout; see `similarity::live`.)
    if target.get("suppressed").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(false) && !json {
        let into = target.get("supersededBy").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
        println!(
            "note: '{id}' is a RETIRED record{} — `bsc ui suppress` kept its id and dropped its content, so there is little left to score.",
            if into.is_empty() { String::new() } else { format!(", superseded by `{into}`") },
        );
    }
    // A record harvested from the target's own source file — or from a barrel/submodule the target is
    // (transitively) part of — is withheld from the ranking (it is the same module wearing another id,
    // not something to merge into — `similarity::harvest_families`). SAY SO: an unexplained absence in a
    // ranked list reads as "nothing resembles it", which is the same failure the retired-record note
    // above exists to prevent. Shape mode scores a different measure and does not withhold.
    if !shape && !json {
        let held = crate::similarity::harvest_siblings_of(&id, &comps);
        if !held.is_empty() {
            println!(
                "note: {} record(s) in the same module/harvest family are not listed ({}) — they are \
                 views of one module (or of a barrel that re-exports it), not duplicates of it.",
                held.len(),
                held.join(", "),
            );
        }
    }
    // #3584: fold each candidate's graph-USAGE (composes-inverse) into the row, so a "these two overlap"
    // proposal arrives with which side is load-bearing — the optimizer folds the LESS-used into the more.
    let idx = used_by_index(&comps);
    let ranked = if shape {
        crate::similarity::rank_shape_similar(&id, &comps, top, floor)
    } else {
        crate::similarity::rank_similar(&id, &comps, top, floor)
    };
    let rows: Vec<serde_json::Value> = ranked
        .into_iter()
        .map(|mut r| {
            let key = (r["kit"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string(), r["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string());
            r["usedBy"] = serde_json::Value::from(idx.get(&key).map_or(0, Vec::len));
            r
        })
        .collect();
    if json {
        let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&rows) } else { serde_json::to_string(&rows) };
        println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        return Ok(());
    }
    if rows.is_empty() {
        println!("no components similar to '{id}'.");
        return Ok(());
    }
    // The shape rows carry different columns because they answer a different question — printing them
    // under `name · contract` headings would report 0.00 for two terms this mode never scored.
    if shape {
        println!("components built like '{id}' (structure only), most-alike first:");
        let fmt = |v: &serde_json::Value| v.as_f64().map_or("—".to_string(), |f| format!("{f:.2}"));
        for r in &rows {
            println!(
                "  {:>3.0}%  {} ({})  [composes {} · skeleton {} · used-by {}]",
                r["score"].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0) * 100.0,
                r["name"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                r["kit"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                fmt(&r["composes_similarity"]),
                fmt(&r["skeleton_similarity"]),
                r["usedBy"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
            );
        }
        return Ok(());
    }
    println!("components similar to '{id}', most-similar first:");
    for r in &rows {
        println!(
            "  {:>3.0}%  {} ({})  [name {:.2} · contract {:.2} · used-by {}]",
            r["score"].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0) * 100.0,
            r["name"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
            r["kit"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
            r["name_similarity"].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0),
            r["contract_similarity"].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0),
            r["usedBy"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
        );
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The composes-INVERSE (#3584): for each `(kitId, name)`, the sorted+deduped names of same-kit components
/// that list it in `composes`. The graph-internal USAGE signal — how load-bearing a component is within its
/// kit — keyed by `(kit, name)` because `composes` resolves by NAME and a name can recur across kits (kits
/// never cross, so a `Button` in kit A and one in kit B are distinct). Computed live from the records, so
/// it is never a placeholder (unlike the codebase-usage `used` field).
fn used_by_index(
    components: &[serde_json::Value],
) -> std::collections::BTreeMap<(String, String), Vec<String>> {
    let mut idx: std::collections::BTreeMap<(String, String), Vec<String>> = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    for c in components {
        let kit = c.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let Some(composer) = c.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) else {
            continue;
        };
        for dep in c.get("composes").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array).into_iter().flatten() {
            if let Some(dep_name) = dep.as_str().filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {
                idx.entry((kit.clone(), dep_name.to_string())).or_default().push(composer.to_string());
            }
        }
    }
    for composers in idx.values_mut() {
        composers.sort();
        composers.dedup();
    }
    idx
}

/// `bsc ui usage-scan` (#3888) — the producer for `used`, and the answer to designer requests #95/#100.
///
/// Walks a DECLARED corpus — `--root DIR` trees plus the kit's own records, always — and reports each
/// component's usage with the source(s) that answered. `--apply` writes `used` + `usageAssessed`.
///
/// The record corpus is not an optimization: post-#3604 the app's modules ARE records, so a scan of the
/// repo tree alone sees one `GraphComponent id=` (the literal `id="x"`) against ten real mount sites.
fn cmd_usage_scan(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut kit, mut apply, mut json, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false, false, false);
    let mut roots: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--kit" => kit = it.next().cloned(),
            "--root" => roots.push(it.next().cloned().ok_or("--root needs a directory")?),
            "--apply" => apply = true,
            "--json" => json = true,
            "--pretty" => { json = true; pretty = true }
            other => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}' (usage: bsc ui usage-scan [--kit K] [--root DIR]... [--apply])")),
        }
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let all: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str(j).ok()).collect();
    let in_scope: Vec<serde_json::Value> = match &kit {
        Some(k) => all.iter().filter(|c| c.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(k.as_str())).cloned().collect(),
        None => all.clone(),
    };

    // ── the corpus ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // The STORE first, and every record of it — a record importing another record is the ordinary case
    // now, so scoping the corpus to `--kit` would hide a cross-kit importer and under-count.
    let mut corpus: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
    for c in &all {
        let id = c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        let mut text = String::new();
        for f in ["srcText", "source"] {
            if let Some(t) = c.get(f).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
                text.push_str(t);
                text.push('\n');
            }
        }
        if !text.trim().is_empty() {
            corpus.push((format!("record:{id}"), text));
        }
    }
    let store_texts = corpus.len();
    let mut files = 0usize;
    for root in &roots {
        walk_source_files(std::path::Path::new(root), &mut |p, text| {
            corpus.push((format!("file:{}", p.display()), text));
            files += 1;
        })?;
    }

    let report = crate::usage_scan::scan(&in_scope, &corpus);
    let examined = report.rows.len();
    let unused = report.unused();
    let with_usage = examined - unused;

    // A SCAN CAN PROVE USE. IT CANNOT PROVE DISUSE.
    //
    // Finding a reference is positive evidence. NOT finding one is evidence only if you know every way a
    // reference can exist — and this scanner was wrong about that twice while it was being written. With
    // three sources, `--apply` authorized deleting `App`, `GraphComponent` and `ThemeProvider`; the
    // fourth source (`src` path) rescued them and left six more, several of which look equally alive.
    //
    // So `usageAssessed` — the flag `doctor --fix` gates pruning on — is written ONLY where usage was
    // actually found. `used` is written for everyone, because the positive counts are the whole point:
    // they collapse 135 of the 192 false dead-root findings this verb exists to fix. A node with no
    // evidence keeps `usageAssessed` absent, stays unprunable, and stays REPORTED — which is the correct
    // reading of "we did not find a reference" until a corpus exists that can justify the stronger claim.
    let mut assessed = 0usize;
    if apply {
        let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(None);
        for row in &report.rows {
            let mut rec = current_record(&store, &row.id)?;
            if rec.is_null() {
                continue;
            }
            let kit = rec.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
            rec["used"] = serde_json::Value::from(row.used);
            if row.used > 0 {
                rec["usageAssessed"] = serde_json::Value::Bool(true);
                assessed += 1;
            }
            stamped_set(&store, &row.id, rec, &writer)?;
            // #110: every other write path emits this right after its `store.set` so the Design Studio's
            // live-focus poll (`useUiActivity`) re-hydrates and the orphan/dangling-branch badges stop
            // lagging the store — this loop was the one write path that never did, so `used`/`usageAssessed`
            // could flip a record from orphan to composed on disk while the running app kept showing the
            // stale badge until a full relaunch.
            bsc_util::emit_ui_activity_in("component", &row.id, &kit);
        }
    }

    if json {
        let out = serde_json::json!({
            "corpus": { "records": store_texts, "files": files, "roots": roots },
            "examined": examined,
            "withUsage": with_usage,
            "unused": unused,
            "applied": apply,
            "assessed": assessed,
            "rows": report.rows.iter().map(|r| serde_json::json!({
                "id": r.id, "name": r.name, "kit": r.kit, "used": r.used,
                "sources": r.sources.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            })).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        });
        let text = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out) } else { serde_json::to_string(&out) };
        println!("{}", text.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        return Ok(());
    }

    // The corpus is printed FIRST and always. A usage number whose scope the reader has to infer is the
    // failure mode this verb exists to end, not one to reproduce in its own output.
    println!("corpus: {store_texts} record(s) + {files} file(s) from {} root(s){}", roots.len(),
        if roots.is_empty() { " — records only; pass --root to add a tree" } else { "" });
    for r in &roots {
        println!("  root: {r}");
    }
    println!("examined {examined} component(s): {with_usage} with usage, {unused} with none");
    for row in report.rows.iter().filter(|r| r.used > 0).take(40) {
        let srcs: Vec<&str> = row.sources.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
        println!("  {:>4}  {} ({})  [{}]", row.used, row.name, row.id, srcs.join(" · "));
    }
    if with_usage > 40 {
        println!("  … {} more with usage (use --json for all)", with_usage - 40);
    }
    if apply {
        println!("applied: wrote `used` to {examined} record(s); `usageAssessed` to the {assessed} with evidence of use");
        println!(
            "  the other {unused} keep NO assessment on purpose — a scan proves USE, never DISUSE, so \
             they stay reported and unprunable rather than becoming deletable by default"
        );
    } else {
        println!("(read only — pass --apply to write `used`, and `usageAssessed` for the {with_usage} with evidence)");
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Walk `root` for TS/TSX/JS/JSX sources, handing each `(path, text)` to `f`. A missing root is an
/// ERROR, not an empty walk: a mistyped `--root` that silently contributes nothing would report every
/// component in that tree as unused, and `--apply` would then mark them assessed.
fn walk_source_files(
    root: &std::path::Path,
    f: &mut impl FnMut(&std::path::Path, String),
) -> Result<(), String> {
    if !root.exists() {
        return Err(format!("--root '{}' does not exist — a root that contributes nothing would report its components unused", root.display()));
    }
    let mut stack = vec![root.to_path_buf()];
    while let Some(dir) = stack.pop() {
        let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(&dir) {
            Ok(e) => e,
            Err(_) => continue,
        };
        for entry in entries.flatten() {
            let p = entry.path();
            let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
            if p.is_dir() {
                // Never walk into a build output or a dependency tree — they hold megabytes of code that
                // says nothing about whether THIS library's components are used.
                if !matches!(name.as_str(), "node_modules" | "target" | "dist" | ".git" | ".bsc-records") {
                    stack.push(p);
                }
            } else if matches!(
                p.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()),
                Some("ts" | "tsx" | "js" | "jsx")
            ) {
                if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(&p) {
                    f(&p, text);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui used-by <id>` / `--all` (#3584) — the graph-usage read (composes-inverse). A READ verb, never
/// scope-gated. Single form: one component's composers + count. `--all`: every component ranked by usage,
/// most-used first (`--kit` scopes to one kit) — the whole-library "what is load-bearing" view.
fn cmd_used_by(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut json, mut pretty, mut all, mut kit_filter, mut id) =
        (None::<String>, false, false, false, None::<String>, None::<String>);
    // `--src` adds the LITERAL reference count beside the composes-inverse one. The two together are what
    // separates a MISSING composes edge (count 0, references > 0) from a real dead root (both 0) — the
    // call every `doctor` dangling-branch/orphan finding needs before anything is deleted.
    let mut src = false;
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--json" => json = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            "--all" => all = true,
            "--src" => src = true,
            "--kit" => kit_filter = it.next().cloned(),
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other if id.is_none() => id = Some(other.to_string()),
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();
    let idx = used_by_index(&comps);
    let count_of = |c: &serde_json::Value| -> usize {
        let key = (
            c.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string(),
            c.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string(),
        );
        idx.get(&key).map_or(0, Vec::len)
    };

    if all {
        // Whole-library ranking, most-used first (id tiebreak for order-stability).
        let mut rows: Vec<serde_json::Value> = comps
            .iter()
            .filter(|c| kit_filter.as_deref().is_none_or(|k| c.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(k)))
            .map(|c| {
                let mut row = serde_json::json!({
                    "id": c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
                    "name": c.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
                    "kit": c.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
                    "count": count_of(c),
                });
                if src {
                    let cid = c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
                    let nm = c.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
                    row["srcCount"] = serde_json::json!(src_reference_rows(&comps, cid, nm).len());
                }
                row
            })
            .collect();
        rows.sort_by(|a, b| {
            b["count"].as_u64().cmp(&a["count"].as_u64()).then_with(|| a["id"].as_str().cmp(&b["id"].as_str()))
        });
        if json {
            let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&rows) } else { serde_json::to_string(&rows) };
            println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        } else {
            println!("components by graph usage (composes-inverse), most-used first:");
            if src {
                println!("  {:>3}  {:>3}  component", "use", "src");
            }
            for r in &rows {
                if src {
                    // A `0  N` row is the interesting one: nothing composes it, yet N components name it.
                    println!(
                        "  {:>3}  {:>3}  {} ({})",
                        r["count"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
                        r["srcCount"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
                        r["name"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                        r["kit"].as_str().unwrap_or("")
                    );
                } else {
                    println!("  {:>3}  {} ({})", r["count"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0), r["name"].as_str().unwrap_or(""), r["kit"].as_str().unwrap_or(""));
                }
            }
        }
        return Ok(());
    }

    let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui used-by <id> [--json]  |  bsc ui used-by --all [--kit K]")?;
    let target = comps
        .iter()
        .find(|c| c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(id.as_str()))
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("no component with id '{id}' (see `bsc ui list --raw`)"))?;
    let key = (
        target.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string(),
        target.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string(),
    );
    let composers = idx.get(&key).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    let src_refs = if src { src_reference_rows(&comps, &id, &key.1) } else { Vec::new() };
    let mut out = serde_json::json!({
        "id": id,
        "name": key.1,
        "kit": key.0,
        "usedBy": composers,
        "count": composers.len(),
    });
    if src {
        out["srcRefs"] = serde_json::Value::Array(src_refs.clone());
        out["srcCount"] = serde_json::json!(src_refs.len());
    }
    if json {
        let text = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out) } else { serde_json::to_string(&out) };
        println!("{}", text.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    } else if composers.is_empty() {
        println!("'{}' ({}) is composed by NOTHING in its kit — an orphan candidate (used-by 0).", key.1, key.0);
        if src {
            // THE DISTINCTION THIS FLAG EXISTS FOR: composed by nothing, yet literally referenced, means a
            // MISSING `composes` edge — not a dead root, and not safe to delete.
            if src_refs.is_empty() {
                println!("  …and no literal srcText reference either — a genuine dead root.");
            } else {
                println!(
                    "  …but {} component(s) literally reference it: {} — a MISSING `composes` edge, not a dead root.",
                    src_refs.len(),
                    src_refs.iter().filter_map(|r| r["name"].as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
                );
            }
        }
    } else {
        println!("'{}' ({}) is composed by {} component(s): {}", key.1, key.0, composers.len(), composers.join(", "));
        if src {
            println!("  literal srcText references: {}", src_refs.len());
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Every OTHER live component whose `srcText`/`source` literally mentions `name`, with the mention kinds
/// broken out — the shared body of `bsc ui refs` and `bsc ui used-by --src`.
///
/// ONE IMPLEMENTATION ON PURPOSE. `used-by` reads the DECLARED composes graph, so a component genuinely
/// used in another's JSX but never added to `composes` reads as an orphan there, indistinguishable from a
/// dead root — which is exactly the call `doctor`'s dangling-branch/orphan findings need made. A second,
/// cruder matcher is why the earlier attempt at this was not landed, so both verbs go through
/// [`crate::usage_scan::name_mentions`] AND through this one loop.
fn src_reference_rows(comps: &[serde_json::Value], id: &str, name: &str) -> Vec<serde_json::Value> {
    let mut hits: Vec<serde_json::Value> = Vec::new();
    if name.is_empty() {
        return hits;
    }
    for c in comps {
        let cid = c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        if cid == id || cid.is_empty() {
            continue; // never a reference to itself
        }
        if c.get("suppressed").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool) == Some(true) {
            continue; // a tombstone's content is gone; it can only ever dilute
        }
        let mut text = String::new();
        for f in ["srcText", "source"] {
            if let Some(t) = c.get(f).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
                text.push_str(t);
                text.push('\n');
            }
        }
        if text.trim().is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let mentions = crate::usage_scan::name_mentions(&text, name);
        if mentions.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let kind = |k: crate::usage_scan::MentionKind| {
            mentions.iter().filter(|m| std::mem::discriminant(*m) == std::mem::discriminant(&k)).count()
        };
        hits.push(serde_json::json!({
            "id": cid,
            "name": c.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
            "kit": c.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
            "jsx": kind(crate::usage_scan::MentionKind::JsxTag),
            "importClause": kind(crate::usage_scan::MentionKind::ImportClause),
            "bare": kind(crate::usage_scan::MentionKind::Bare),
            "total": mentions.len(),
        }));
    }
    hits.sort_by(|a, b| {
        b["total"].as_u64().cmp(&a["total"].as_u64()).then_with(|| a["id"].as_str().cmp(&b["id"].as_str()))
    });
    hits
}

/// `bsc ui refs <id>` (#113) — literal srcText cross-references to a component's NAME, across every
/// OTHER live component in the store. The complement to `used-by`: `used-by` reads the DECLARED
/// composes graph, so a component actually used in another's JSX/import but never added to `composes`
/// reads as an orphan there, indistinguishable from a genuinely dead root. This scans raw srcText for
/// the name itself instead, so the two stop looking identical.
fn cmd_refs(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut json, mut pretty, mut id) = (None::<String>, false, false, None::<String>);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--json" => json = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other if id.is_none() => id = Some(other.to_string()),
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui refs <id> [--json] [--pretty]")?;
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();
    let target = comps
        .iter()
        .find(|c| c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(id.as_str()))
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("no component with id '{id}' (see `bsc ui list --raw`)"))?;
    let name = target.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
    if name.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!("component '{id}' has no name to search for"));
    }

    let hits = src_reference_rows(&comps, &id, &name);

    if json {
        let out = serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "name": name, "refs": hits, "count": hits.len() });
        let text = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out) } else { serde_json::to_string(&out) };
        bsc_util::emit_line(&text.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    } else if hits.is_empty() {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
            "'{name}' ({id}) — no literal srcText reference found in any other component. Genuinely unreferenced, not just missing a `composes` edge.",
        ));
    } else {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("'{name}' ({id}) is literally referenced in {} component(s):", hits.len()));
        for h in &hits {
            bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
                "  {} ({})  [jsx {} · import {} · bare {}]",
                h["name"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                h["id"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                h["jsx"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
                h["importClause"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
                h["bare"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The `bsc ui pattern` verbs (#a-pattern-has-no-id-so-the-only-way-to-author-a-sibling-is-to-copy-one)
/// — a convention with an ID, so authoring the fifth sibling is "add a member to <pattern>" rather than
/// "find one and copy it".
fn cmd_pattern(args: &[String], prog: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let sub = args.first().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("");
    if sub.is_empty() || sub == "help" {
        print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "pattern"));
        return Ok(());
    }
    // TWO stores are in play here, so `--dir` cannot mean both. It keeps its usual meaning — the
    // COMPONENT store, which is what conformance is computed against — and the pattern records get
    // their own flag. Sharing one flag would silently look for patterns inside the component dir.
    let (mut dir, mut pattern_dir, mut json, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false, false);
    let (mut id, mut from, mut name, mut threshold) =
        (None::<String>, None::<String>, None::<String>, crate::patterns::DEFAULT_CONFORMANCE);
    let mut it = args[1..].iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pattern-dir" => pattern_dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--from" => from = it.next().cloned(),
            "--name" => name = it.next().cloned(),
            "--threshold" => {
                threshold = it.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<f64>().ok()).ok_or("--threshold needs a number in [0,1]")?;
            }
            "--json" => json = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other if id.is_none() => id = Some(other.to_string()),
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&threshold) {
        return Err("--threshold must be in [0,1]".to_string());
    }
    let pstore = open_pattern_store(&pattern_dir)?;
    let cstore = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        cstore.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();
    let emit = |v: &serde_json::Value| -> Result<(), String> {
        let t = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(v) } else { serde_json::to_string(v) };
        println!("{}", t.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        Ok(())
    };
    let read = |id: &str| -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
        pstore
            .get(id)?
            .as_deref()
            .and_then(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok())
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("no pattern with id '{id}' (see `bsc ui pattern list`)"))
    };

    match sub {
        "list" => {
            let rows: Vec<serde_json::Value> = pstore
                .list()
                .iter()
                .filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok())
                .map(|p| {
                    let n = crate::patterns::conforming(&p, &comps, true).len();
                    serde_json::json!({
                        "id": p["id"], "name": p["name"],
                        "signatureSource": p["signatureSource"], "members": n,
                    })
                })
                .collect();
            if json {
                return emit(&serde_json::Value::Array(rows));
            }
            if rows.is_empty() {
                println!("No named patterns yet. Find the library's conventions with `bsc ui patterns`, then promote one:");
                println!("  bsc ui pattern new <id> --from <a-member-id>");
                return Ok(());
            }
            for r in &rows {
                println!(
                    "  {:<28} {:>3} members  [{}]  {}",
                    r["id"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                    r["members"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
                    r["signatureSource"].as_str().unwrap_or("?"),
                    r["name"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                );
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        "get" => {
            let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui pattern get <id>")?;
            let p = read(&id)?;
            let members = crate::patterns::conforming(&p, &comps, true);
            let rows: Vec<serde_json::Value> = members
                .iter()
                .map(|m| serde_json::json!({
                    "id": m.id, "name": m.name, "kit": m.kit, "exemplar": m.exemplar,
                    "basis": m.basis.as_str(),
                    "score": m.score.map(|s| (s * 100.0).round() / 100.0),
                }))
                .collect();
            if json {
                let mut out = p.clone();
                out["members"] = serde_json::Value::Array(rows);
                return emit(&out);
            }
            println!("{}  —  {}", p["id"].as_str().unwrap_or(""), p["name"].as_str().unwrap_or(""));
            let list = |v: &serde_json::Value| {
                v.as_array().map(|a| a.iter().filter_map(|x| x.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")).unwrap_or_default()
            };
            println!("  signature ({}):", p["signatureSource"].as_str().unwrap_or("?"));
            println!("    composes: {}", nonempty(&list(&p["signature"]["composes"])));
            println!("    renders:  {}", nonempty(&list(&p["signature"]["skeleton"])));
            let basis = members.first().map(|m| m.basis.as_str()).unwrap_or("scored");
            println!("\n  {} member(s), matched by {basis}:", members.len());
            for m in &members {
                println!(
                    "    {}{}{}",
                    m.name,
                    if m.exemplar { "  (exemplar)" } else { "" },
                    m.score.map(|s| format!("  {:.0}%", s * 100.0)).unwrap_or_default(),
                );
            }
            if basis == "containment" {
                println!(
                    "\n  NOTE: matched by CONTAINMENT of a declared signature, which is looser than scoring\n  against exemplars — anything holding these parts matches. Promote a real member with\n  `bsc ui pattern new {} --from <id>` to tighten it.",
                    p["id"].as_str().unwrap_or("<id>"),
                );
            }
            println!("\n  To author into this pattern, read an exemplar: `bsc ui get <exemplar-id>`");
            Ok(())
        }
        "new" => {
            let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui pattern new <id> --from <member-id> [--name \"...\"]")?;
            let from = from.ok_or(
                "bsc ui pattern new needs --from <member-id>: a pattern is PROMOTED from a cluster `bsc ui patterns` found, and any one member names it",
            )?;
            if pstore.get(&id)?.is_some() {
                return Err(format!("a pattern with id '{id}' already exists — `bsc ui pattern get {id}`, or pick another id"));
            }
            // The cluster holding <from> IS the pattern. Reusing the sweep means a promoted pattern's
            // members are the cluster that was reported, not a differently-drawn set.
            let clusters = crate::similarity::shape_clusters(&comps, threshold, 2);
            let cluster = clusters
                .iter()
                .find(|c| {
                    c["members"].as_array().is_some_and(|a| {
                        a.iter().any(|m| m["id"].as_str() == Some(from.as_str()))
                    })
                })
                .ok_or_else(|| format!(
                    "'{from}' is not in any cluster at threshold {threshold} — nothing to promote. Check `bsc ui patterns --threshold {threshold}`, or lower the bar."
                ))?;
            let member_ids: Vec<&str> =
                cluster["members"].as_array().into_iter().flatten().filter_map(|m| m["id"].as_str()).collect();
            let members: Vec<serde_json::Value> = comps
                .iter()
                .filter(|c| member_ids.contains(&c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("")))
                .cloned()
                .collect();
            let display = name.unwrap_or_else(|| id.clone());
            let rec = crate::patterns::derive(&id, &display, &members, threshold);
            pstore.set(&id, &serde_json::to_string(&rec).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?)?;
            if json {
                return emit(&rec);
            }
            println!("{id}  —  promoted from the cluster containing '{from}' ({} exemplars)", members.len());
            println!("  bsc ui pattern get {id}");
            Ok(())
        }
        "remove" => {
            let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui pattern remove <id>")?;
            read(&id)?; // a removal of nothing is an error, not a silent success
            pstore.remove(&id)?;
            println!("{id} removed");
            Ok(())
        }
        "of" => {
            // The REVERSE lookup: which convention does this record already belong to? The read a
            // session makes when it has a component in hand, not a pattern.
            let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui pattern of <component-id>")?;
            if !comps.iter().any(|c| c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(id.as_str())) {
                return Err(format!("no component with id '{id}' (see `bsc ui list --raw`)"));
            }
            let hits: Vec<serde_json::Value> = pstore
                .list()
                .iter()
                .filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok())
                .filter_map(|p| {
                    let m = crate::patterns::conforming(&p, &comps, true);
                    m.iter().find(|c| c.id == id).map(|c| serde_json::json!({
                        "pattern": p["id"], "name": p["name"], "basis": c.basis.as_str(),
                        "score": c.score.map(|s| (s * 100.0).round() / 100.0), "exemplar": c.exemplar,
                    }))
                })
                .collect();
            if json {
                return emit(&serde_json::Value::Array(hits));
            }
            if hits.is_empty() {
                println!("'{id}' belongs to no named pattern.");
                println!("  If it should: `bsc ui similar {id} --shape` to see what it is built like,");
                println!("  then `bsc ui pattern new <pattern-id> --from {id}` to name the convention.");
                return Ok(());
            }
            for h in &hits {
                println!(
                    "  {} ({}){}",
                    h["pattern"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                    h["basis"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                    if h["exemplar"].as_bool().unwrap_or(false) { "  — an exemplar" } else { "" },
                );
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        other => Err(format!("unknown `pattern` command '{other}' — try list | get | new | remove | of")),
    }
}

fn nonempty(s: &str) -> String {
    if s.is_empty() { "—".to_string() } else { s.to_string() }
}

fn open_pattern_store(dir: &Option<String>) -> Result<bsc_json_store::Store, String> {
    let dir = bsc_cli_util::resolve_store_path(dir, "BSC_COMPONENT_PATTERN_DIR", || {
        bsc_util::bsc_base_dir()
            .map(|b| b.join("patterns"))
            .ok_or_else(|| "could not resolve a home directory; set HOME/USERPROFILE".to_string())
    })?;
    Ok(bsc_json_store::Store::new(dir, "pattern"))
}

/// `bsc ui patterns` — the whole-library shape sweep
/// (#shape-similarity-is-pairwise-so-a-pattern-can-only-be-confirmed-never-found).
///
/// `similar --shape` needs a seed, so it can only CONFIRM a pattern someone already suspects. This
/// returns the equivalence classes themselves. Prints the threshold and the counts before the rows —
/// a sweep whose bar is invisible reads as "this is everything".
fn cmd_patterns(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut json, mut pretty, mut kit_filter) = (None::<String>, false, false, None::<String>);
    let (mut threshold, mut min_size) = (PATTERN_THRESHOLD, 2usize);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--kit" => kit_filter = it.next().cloned(),
            "--threshold" => {
                threshold = it.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<f64>().ok()).ok_or("--threshold needs a number in [0,1]")?;
            }
            "--min" => {
                min_size = it.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<usize>().ok()).filter(|n| *n >= 2)
                    .ok_or("--min needs an integer of 2 or more (a cluster of one is not a pattern)")?;
            }
            "--json" => json = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&threshold) {
        return Err("--threshold must be in [0,1]".to_string());
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> = store
        .list()
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok())
        .filter(|c| kit_filter.as_deref().is_none_or(|k| c.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(k)))
        .collect();
    let clusters = crate::similarity::shape_clusters(&comps, threshold, min_size);
    if json {
        let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&clusters) } else { serde_json::to_string(&clusters) };
        println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        return Ok(());
    }
    let clustered: usize = clusters.iter().filter_map(|c| c["size"].as_u64()).sum::<u64>() as usize;
    println!(
        "{} structural pattern(s) over {} record(s) — {} of {} scanned are in one, at threshold {threshold:.2} (min {min_size}).",
        clusters.len(),
        clustered,
        clustered,
        comps.len(),
    );
    if clusters.is_empty() {
        println!("Nothing clusters at that bar. Lower --threshold to see looser groupings.");
        return Ok(());
    }
    for c in &clusters {
        let sig = &c["signature"];
        let list = |v: &serde_json::Value| {
            v.as_array().map(|a| a.iter().filter_map(|x| x.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")).unwrap_or_default()
        };
        let (composes, skeleton) = (list(&sig["composes"]), list(&sig["skeleton"]));
        let cohesion = c["cohesion"].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0);
        println!(
            "\n  {} members · cohesion {:.0}%{}",
            c["size"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
            cohesion * 100.0,
            // Connected components chain; below the bar the group is related, not uniform.
            if cohesion + 1e-9 < threshold { "  ← CHAINED (some members are not alike)" } else { "" },
        );
        println!("    composes: {}", if composes.is_empty() { "—".into() } else { composes });
        println!("    renders:  {}", if skeleton.is_empty() { "—".into() } else { skeleton });
        let names: Vec<&str> =
            c["members"].as_array().into_iter().flatten().filter_map(|m| m["name"].as_str()).collect();
        println!("    {}", names.join(", "));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui exports` (#a-record-holds-one-item-not-a-module-of-them) — a record's PUBLIC SURFACE, grouped
/// into the ITEMS its exports name.
///
/// The read behind the library's one-record-one-item rule, and the one nothing else could answer:
