            .unwrap();

        let err = replace_src(&store, "consolepage", unbuildable, None).unwrap_err();

        assert_eq!(rec["srcText"], buildable, "the refused write left srcText untouched");

        assert!(replace_src(&store, "consolepage", unbuildable, None).is_ok(), "provides beats the preview sandbox");

        // And `--force` overrides it even without `provides`, on a fresh record.
        store.set("kitsharemodal", r#"{"id":"kitsharemodal","name":"KitShareModal","srcText":"export const K = () => null;"}"#).unwrap();
        FORCE_WRITE.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
        let forced = replace_src(&store, "kitsharemodal", unbuildable, None);
        FORCE_WRITE.store(false, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);

    }

    /// #119 — the half `refuse_buildable_regression` cannot see. That guard asks whether the NEW source
    /// still builds, so an anonymous overwrite that happens to stay buildable sails through it while
    /// still destroying a named author's work. `kitsharemodal` rev4-6 and `consolepage` rev11-12 were
    /// both lost that way. Every source here is buildable, precisely so the other guard stays silent
    /// and this one is the only thing under test.
    #[test]
    fn an_unattributed_write_cannot_clobber_srctext_someone_signed_for() {
        let dir = tmp_store_dir("anon-src-overwrite");
        let store = bsc_json_store::Store::new(dir, "component");
        let designer_src = "export const KitShareModal = () => null;";
        store
            .set(
                "kitsharemodal",
                &format!(
                    r#"{{"id":"kitsharemodal","name":"KitShareModal","srcText":{},
                        "history":[{{"rev":1,"by":"designer","changed":["srcText"]}}]}}"#,
                    serde_json::to_string(designer_src).unwrap()
                ),
            )
            .unwrap();
        let other = "export const KitShareModal = () => 1;";

        // The filed shape: an anonymous sync overwrites a designer's source.
        let err = replace_src(&store, "kitsharemodal", other, None).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("UNATTRIBUTED"), "{err}");
        assert!(err.contains("designer"), "it must name whose work is at risk: {err}");
        let rec: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&store.get("kitsharemodal").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rec["srcText"], designer_src, "the refused write left srcText untouched");

        // An ATTRIBUTED write passes — any name, not just the prior one. Identifying yourself is the
        // whole ask; the guard is not an ownership lock.
        replace_src(&store, "kitsharemodal", other, Some("harvester")).unwrap();
        let rec: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&store.get("kitsharemodal").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rec["srcText"], other);
        assert_eq!(rec["updatedBy"], "harvester", "--by flows through to the stamp");
    }

    /// The escapes and the non-cases, kept separate so a failure names which rule broke.
    #[test]
    fn the_anonymous_srctext_guard_stays_out_of_the_way_of_everything_else() {
        use serde_json::json;
        let signed = json!({
            "id": "c", "srcText": "export const C = () => null;",
            "history": [{ "rev": 1, "by": "designer", "changed": ["srcText"] }],
        });

        // --force is the deliberate override.
        assert!(refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite("c", &signed, "next", "unknown", true).is_ok());
        // Identical content loses nothing, so there is nothing to refuse.
        assert!(
            refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite("c", &signed, "export const C = () => null;", "unknown", false)
                .is_ok()
        );
        // Nobody to protect: the prior write was itself unattributed.
        let anon = json!({
            "id": "c", "srcText": "x",
            "history": [{ "rev": 1, "by": "unknown", "changed": ["srcText"] }],
        });
        assert!(refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite("c", &anon, "y", "unknown", false).is_ok());
        // No history at all, and history that never moved srcText — nothing recorded to protect.
        assert!(refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite("c", &json!({ "id": "c" }), "y", "unknown", false).is_ok());
        let namesonly = json!({
            "id": "c", "srcText": "x",
            "history": [{ "rev": 1, "by": "designer", "changed": ["name"] }],
        });
        assert!(refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite("c", &namesonly, "y", "unknown", false).is_ok());

        // A `created` entry DOES count when the record carries srcText — a record authored with its
        // source and never rewritten is exactly the newly-authored Design Studio record this protects.
        let created = json!({
            "id": "c", "srcText": "export const C = () => null;",
            "history": [{ "rev": 1, "by": "designer", "changed": ["created"] }],
        });
        assert!(refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite("c", &created, "y", "unknown", false).is_err());
        // ...but not on a record with no source of its own — there was never any srcText authored.
        let created_srcless =
            json!({ "id": "c", "history": [{ "rev": 1, "by": "designer", "changed": ["created"] }] });
        assert!(refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite("c", &created_srcless, "y", "unknown", false).is_ok());
    }

    /// REGRESSION, designer request #91. A broken-`composes` bug was filed that was not one, because
    /// `bsc ui get deploytoggle` answered a bare `null` for a record present under id `toggle` with name
    /// `DeployToggle`. The lookup is the bug; the graph was correct.
    #[test]
    fn get_resolves_a_name_as_well_as_an_id_and_refuses_to_answer_null() {

        let store = bsc_json_store::Store::new(dir.clone(), "component");
        store.set("toggle", r#"{"id":"toggle","name":"DeployToggle","kitId":"k"}"#).unwrap();
        let go = |a: Vec<&str>| run(a.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect(), "bsc ui");

        // The id path is untouched.
        assert!(go(vec!["get", "toggle", "--dir", &dir]).is_ok());
        // The reporter's EXACT command now resolves — by name, case-insensitively, through both the plain

        assert!(go(vec!["get", "deploytoggle", "--field", "id", "--dir", &dir]).is_ok(), "and with --field");

        // A genuine miss is an ERROR, not `null` on stdout — that silence is what made the graph look broken.
        let err = go(vec!["get", "nosuchthing", "--dir", &dir]).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("nosuchthing"), "{err}");

        store.set("toggle2", r#"{"id":"toggle2","name":"DeployToggle","kitId":"k"}"#).unwrap();
        let err = resolve_component_handle(&store, "DeployToggle").unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("toggle") && err.contains("toggle2"), "names both candidates: {err}");
    }

            // The traversal defence refuses a non-bare --out name.
            let err = run(vec!["get".into(), "fleetpage".into(), "--field".into(), "srcText".into(),
                              "--out".into(), "../escape".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()], "bsc ui").unwrap_err();
            assert!(err.contains("BARE FILENAME"), "a path traversal is refused: {err}");
        });
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&scratch);
    }

    #[test]
    fn granular_writes_refuse_under_a_read_ui_scope_before_stdin_or_the_store() {
        // #3382: the read-only scope is THREAD-LOCAL — no process env, so this refusal
        // test cannot leak into any test running beside it.
        bsc_cli_util::with_scopes(Some(r#"{"ui":"read"}"#), || {
            // set-src is a MUTATION: it refuses at the write-scope gate BEFORE reading stdin (so no --dir /

            let err = run(vec!["set-src".into(), "x".into()], "bsc ui").unwrap_err();
            assert!(err.contains("'ui'") && err.contains("read-only"), "set-src read-scope refusal: {err}");
            // patch refuses the same way, before the store is touched.
            let err = run(vec!["patch".into(), "x".into(), "/name".into(), "Button".into()], "bsc ui").unwrap_err();
            assert!(err.contains("'ui'") && err.contains("read-only"), "patch read-scope refusal: {err}");
            // `get --field` is a READ — reachable under the read scope (against a scratch --dir).
            let dir = tmp_store_dir("granular-read-scope");
            bsc_json_store::Store::new(dir.clone(), "component")
                .set("card", r#"{"id":"card","name":"Card"}"#)

            assert!(run(vec!["patch".into(), "help".into()], "bsc ui").is_ok());

    // ── record history / attribution / optimistic concurrency (#3164) ────────────────────────────

    /// A scratch COMPONENT store over a fresh temp dir, for the stamping tests.
    fn tmp_component_store(tag: &str) -> bsc_json_store::Store {
        bsc_json_store::Store::new(tmp_store_dir(tag), "component")
    }

    /// Parse a stored record's verbatim JSON back to a `Value` (the read-back the assertions use).
    fn stored(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, id: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
        serde_json::from_str(&store.get(id).unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap()
    }

    /// The record #4197 exists for: a PAGE whose source file no longer exists (`fleetpage`, deleted by
    /// #3636), so the store holds the only copy of that UI and a dropped field is unrecoverable.
    fn fleetpage_record() -> serde_json::Value {
        serde_json::json!({
            "id": "fleetpage", "name": "FleetPage", "kitId": "base-studio-code", "role": "page",
            "composes": ["Row", "Card"], "src": "src/features/planner/fleet/Fleet.tsx",
            "folder": "features/planner/fleet", "srcText": "old",
            "props": { "title": "string" },
        })
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_partial_write_merges_and_preserves_every_field_it_omitted() {
        // THE regression test for #4197. `set` used to REPLACE, so the write below — the exact shape the
        // worker protocol tells a fleet worker to make for a record-backed component file (#4193) —
        // deleted the record's kit, role, composes edges, provenance and props. Against the old
        // behaviour every `preserved` assertion fails; against the merge (the #4154 semantics, now shared
        // with `bsc graph impl set`) only `srcText` moves.
        let store = tmp_component_store("merge-partial");
        let rich = fleetpage_record();
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rich), None, "seed", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();

        let partial = serde_json::json!({ "id": "fleetpage", "srcText": "new" });
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&partial), None, "worker", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();

        let after = stored(&store, "fleetpage");
        assert_eq!(after["srcText"], "new", "the supplied field is written");
        for (field, expected) in [
            ("name", serde_json::json!("FleetPage")),
            ("kitId", serde_json::json!("base-studio-code")),
            ("role", serde_json::json!("page")),
            ("composes", serde_json::json!(["Row", "Card"])),
            ("src", serde_json::json!("src/features/planner/fleet/Fleet.tsx")),
            ("folder", serde_json::json!("features/planner/fleet")),
            ("props", serde_json::json!({ "title": "string" })),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(after[field], expected, "the write never mentioned {field}, so it is preserved");
        }
        // The history reflects the truth: an EDIT, with nothing dropped.
        let entry = after["history"].as_array().unwrap().last().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(entry["changed"], serde_json::json!(["srcText"]), "only srcText moved: {entry}");
        assert!(entry.get("dropped").is_none(), "a merging write removes nothing: {entry}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn clear_removes_one_field_explicitly_and_leaves_the_rest_alone() {
        // A merge makes removal-by-omission impossible, so removal is EXPLICIT — `--clear a,b`, exactly
        // as `bsc graph impl set` spells it (#4154). The removal is recorded in the history's `dropped`.
        let store = tmp_component_store("merge-clear");
        let rich = fleetpage_record();
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rich), None, "seed", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        let prior = stored(&store, "fleetpage");

        let clear = ["folder".to_string()];
        let edit = serde_json::json!({ "id": "fleetpage", "srcText": "new" });
        let plan = WritePlan { replace: false, clear: &clear };
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&edit), None, "designer", "component", None, plan).unwrap();

        let after = stored(&store, "fleetpage");
        assert!(after.get("folder").is_none(), "the cleared field is gone");
        assert_eq!(after["src"], "src/features/planner/fleet/Fleet.tsx", "its neighbours are untouched");
        assert_eq!(after["composes"], serde_json::json!(["Row", "Card"]));
        let entry = after["history"].as_array().unwrap().last().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(entry["dropped"], serde_json::json!(["folder"]), "the removal is legible in `bsc ui log`: {entry}");
        // An asked-for removal is NOT warned about — the caller requested it, and warning about a deletion
        // you just asked for is the noise that trains people to ignore the real warning.
        let effective = crate::record::merge_over(&prior, &edit, &clear);
        assert!(destructive_write_warning("fleetpage", "component", &prior, &effective, &clear).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_replace_write_still_replaces_and_warns_about_every_field_it_deletes() {
        // `--replace` is the ONE remaining way to delete by omission — it exists for the app bridge,
        // `bsc ui import`, and the seed reconcile's authoritative reset (#3723), which a merge would stop
        // from ever converging. Because it can still lose data, it says so, naming each field.
        let store = tmp_component_store("replace-warns");
        let rich = fleetpage_record();
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rich), None, "seed", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        let prior = stored(&store, "fleetpage");

        let partial = serde_json::json!({ "id": "fleetpage", "srcText": "new" });
        let plan = WritePlan { replace: true, clear: &[] };
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&partial), None, "bridge", "component", None, plan).unwrap();
        let after = stored(&store, "fleetpage");
        assert!(after.get("kitId").is_none() && after.get("composes").is_none(), "--replace really replaces");

        let msg = destructive_write_warning("fleetpage", "component", &prior, &partial, &[])
            .expect("a partial --replace over a rich record is destructive");
        for field in ["composes", "folder", "kitId", "name", "props", "role", "src"] {
            assert!(msg.contains(field), "the warning names {field}: {msg}");
        }
        // …and NOT the server-managed fields, which every write re-stamps regardless of the payload.
        // Reporting those would fire on every single write and train the reader to ignore it.
        for noise in ["rev", "updatedAt", "updatedBy", "history"] {
            assert!(!msg.contains(&format!(" {noise},")) && !msg.contains(&format!(" {noise}.")),
                "the warning does not cry wolf about {noise}: {msg}");
        }
    }

        let args: Vec<String> =

        let bare: Vec<String> = vec!["--clear".to_string()];
        assert!(cmd_set(&bare, open_component_store, validate_component_batch, "component")
            .unwrap_err()
            .contains("--clear needs a comma-separated field list"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_destructive_write_is_recorded_in_the_history_separately_from_edits() {
        // `changed` already counts a removal, but files it next to ordinary edits — so `bsc ui log` could
        // not tell "deleted half the record" from "fixed a typo". `dropped` is what makes that legible,
        // and it is ABSENT on a non-destructive write so existing entries keep their shape.
        let store = tmp_component_store("drop-history");
        let rich = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "card", "name": "Card", "kitId": "react-ui", "role": "composite", "composes": ["Row"],
        });
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rich), None, "seed", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        let first: serde_json::Value = stored(&store, "card");
        let entry = first["history"].as_array().unwrap().last().unwrap();
        assert!(entry.get("dropped").is_none(), "a create drops nothing: {entry}");

        let partial = serde_json::json!({ "id": "card", "name": "Card" });
        let plan = WritePlan { replace: true, clear: &[] };
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&partial), None, "designer", "component", None, plan).unwrap();
        let after: serde_json::Value = stored(&store, "card");
        let entry = after["history"].as_array().unwrap().last().unwrap();
        let dropped: Vec<&str> =
            entry["dropped"].as_array().unwrap().iter().map(|v| v.as_str().unwrap()).collect();
        assert_eq!(dropped, vec!["composes", "kitId", "role"]);
        // …and the fields really are gone from the stored record — the warning describes a real deletion,
        // it does not merely predict one.
        assert!(after.get("composes").is_none() && after.get("role").is_none());
    }

    /// The valid-JSX source the write-time syntax gate accepts, parameterised so two revisions differ.
    fn page_src(marker: &str) -> String {
        format!("export function GraphPrimitive() {{ return <div>{marker}</div>; }}\n")
    }

    #[test]
    fn revert_restores_the_source_a_bad_write_replaced() {
        // THE incident, end to end through the store. `graphprimitive` had no packaged seed, so once the
        // designer overwrote it at 01:39 the broken version was the only copy that had ever existed.
        let store = tmp_component_store("revert-restores");
        let good = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "graphprimitive", "name": "GraphPrimitive", "kitId": "base-studio-code",
            "role": "primitive", "provides": "@/shared/ui/spec/graphPrimitive", "srcText": page_src("good"),
        });
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&good), None, "seed", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        let broken = serde_json::json!({ "id": "graphprimitive", "srcText": page_src("broken") });
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&broken), None, "designer", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(stored(&store, "graphprimitive")["srcText"], page_src("broken"));

        cmd_revert(&["graphprimitive".into(), "--dir".into(), store.dir().to_string_lossy().to_string(), "--by".into(), "rescue".into()]).unwrap();

        let after = stored(&store, "graphprimitive");
        assert_eq!(after["srcText"], page_src("good"), "the source the bad write replaced is back");
        assert_eq!(after["rev"], serde_json::json!(3), "a revert is a WRITE — it stamps forward, never rewinds rev");
        assert_eq!(after["updatedBy"], "rescue");
        // Every other field is untouched — a revert of a bad SOURCE must not also rewind good metadata.
        assert_eq!(after["provides"], "@/shared/ui/spec/graphPrimitive");
        assert_eq!(after["role"], "primitive");
        // ...and the version it replaced is itself revertible now, so a mistaken revert is not terminal.
        let entry = after["history"].as_array().unwrap().last().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(entry["prevSrc"], page_src("broken"));
        assert!(entry["note"].as_str().unwrap().starts_with("revert: srcText restored to rev 1"), "{entry}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn revert_to_an_explicit_rev_and_a_refusal_when_it_is_out_of_reach() {
        let store = tmp_component_store("revert-to-rev");
        let mut rec = serde_json::json!({ "id": "kitrenderer", "srcText": page_src("v0") });
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), None, "seed", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        for i in 1..=(crate::record::PREV_SRC_CAP + 2) {
            rec = serde_json::json!({ "id": "kitrenderer", "srcText": page_src(&format!("v{i}")) });
            set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), None, "designer", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        }
        let dir = store.dir().to_string_lossy().to_string();
        let latest = crate::record::read_rev(&stored(&store, "kitrenderer"));

        // An explicit --to inside the retained window lands on exactly that revision's source.
        cmd_revert(&["kitrenderer".into(), "--to".into(), (latest - 2).to_string(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(stored(&store, "kitrenderer")["srcText"], page_src(&format!("v{}", latest - 3)));

        // Past the content cap it REFUSES, and names what is still reachable — it never silently lands on
        // a nearer version, which would report success while restoring bytes that revision never held.
        let err = cmd_revert(&["kitrenderer".into(), "--to".into(), "1".into(), "--dir".into(), dir]).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("no longer retained"), "{err}");
        assert!(err.contains("revertible revisions:"), "the refusal says what IS possible: {err}");
    }

    fn revert_refuses_a_record_with_nothing_to_go_back_to() {
        let store = tmp_component_store("revert-nothing");

        let err = cmd_revert(&["insights".into(), "--dir".into(), store.dir().to_string_lossy().to_string()]).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("no retained earlier source"), "{err}");

        assert_eq!(crate::record::read_rev(&stored(&store, "insights")), 1);

        let err = cmd_revert(&["nosuch".into(), "--dir".into(), store.dir().to_string_lossy().to_string()]).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("nothing to revert"), "{err}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn set_stamped_bumps_rev_and_stamps_attribution_on_each_write() {
        let store = tmp_component_store("stamp-bump");
        let rec = serde_json::json!({ "id": "button", "name": "Button", "kitId": "react-ui" });

        // First write of a brand-new record → rev 1, updatedBy = the writer, updatedAt an ISO stamp.
        let ids = set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), None, "alice", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(ids, vec!["button".to_string()]);
        let s = stored(&store, "button");
        assert_eq!(s["rev"], serde_json::json!(1), "a fresh record's first write is rev 1");
        assert_eq!(s["updatedBy"], "alice");
        assert!(s["updatedAt"].as_str().is_some_and(|t| t.ends_with('Z')), "updatedAt is an ISO stamp");
        // Stamping never disturbs the domain fields.
        assert_eq!(s["name"], "Button");
        assert_eq!(s["kitId"], "react-ui");

        // A second write of the same id bumps from the STORED rev (1 → 2), even though the payload carries none.
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), None, "bob", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        let s = stored(&store, "button");
        assert_eq!(s["rev"], serde_json::json!(2), "the second write bumps to rev 2");
        assert_eq!(s["updatedBy"], "bob", "attribution follows the latest writer");
    }

    #[test]
    fn set_stamped_if_version_rejects_a_stale_write_and_allows_a_current_one() {
        let store = tmp_component_store("stamp-ifver");
        let rec = serde_json::json!({ "id": "chip", "name": "Chip" });
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), None, "x", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap(); // → rev 1

        // --if-version 0 is STALE (current rev is 1): rejected with a clear message, nothing overwritten.
        let err = set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), Some(0), "x", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("version conflict") && err.contains("rev is 1"), "clear conflict message: {err}");
        assert_eq!(stored(&store, "chip")["rev"], serde_json::json!(1), "the stale write did NOT clobber");

        // --if-version 1 matches the current rev → the write lands and bumps to 2.
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), Some(1), "x", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();

        // #4072 — the Design Studio hydrated its graph with `--full`: 1.72 MB over 321 components, of
        // which 77.6% is `srcText` that no node reads, and the page blocked up to 8s on it. The graph
        // projection must carry the node card + `composes` (edges) and NOTHING heavy.
        let store = tmp_component_store("graphproj");
        let dir = store.dir().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        let rec = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "card", "name": "Card", "kitId": "react-ui", "role": "layout", "folder": "pages",
            "used": 12, "composes": ["Box", "Text"],
            // The weight the projection exists to leave behind:
            "srcText": "export function Card() { /* … a great many bytes … */ }",
            "tests": ["a", "b"], "history": [{ "rev": 1 }], "props": { "title": "string" },
        });
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), None, "designer", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();

        let g = bsc_json_store::cli::lean_meta(&store.get("card").unwrap().unwrap(), COMPONENT_SPEC.graph_fields);
        assert_eq!(
            g,
            serde_json::json!({
                "id": "card", "name": "Card", "kitId": "react-ui", "role": "layout",
                "folder": "pages", "used": 12, "composes": ["Box", "Text"]
            })
        );
        // The heavy fields are absent, not merely empty — that is the whole point.
        for heavy in ["srcText", "tests", "history", "props"] {
            assert!(g.get(heavy).is_none(), "{heavy} must not ride the graph projection");
        }
        // And it runs clean end-to-end.
        assert!(run(vec!["list".into(), "--graph".into(), "--dir".into(), dir], "bsc ui").is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn pattern_promotes_a_cluster_then_answers_membership_both_ways() {
        let store = tmp_component_store("pattern-c");
        let pdir = tmp_component_store("pattern-p");
        let (cd, pd) = (store.dir().to_string_lossy().into_owned(), pdir.dir().to_string_lossy().into_owned());
        let card = |id: &str, name: &str| {
            serde_json::json!({
                "id": id, "name": name, "kitId": "react-ui", "role": "composite", "composes": ["Card", "ToggleRow"],
                "srcText": format!("export const {name} = () => <Card title=\"x\"><ToggleRow on={{a}} onToggle={{b}} title=\"t\"/></Card>;"),
            })
        };
        for r in [card("a", "AlphaCard"), card("b", "BetaCard"), card("c", "GammaCard")] {
            store.set(r["id"].as_str().unwrap(), &r.to_string()).unwrap();
        }
        let d = |extra: &[&str]| {
            extra.iter().map(|s| s.to_string())
                .chain(["--dir".into(), cd.clone(), "--pattern-dir".into(), pd.clone()])
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        };
        // An empty store lists cleanly and points at how to fill it, rather than printing nothing.
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "list"]), "bsc ui").is_ok());
        // Promotion needs --from: there is no positional cluster index, because one would go stale.
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "new", "settings-toggle-card"]), "bsc ui").is_err(), "--from is required");
        let err = run(d(&["pattern", "new", "p", "--from", "ghost"]), "bsc ui").unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("not in any cluster"), "{err}");

        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "new", "settings-toggle-card", "--from", "a", "--name", "Settings toggle card"]), "bsc ui").is_ok());
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "new", "settings-toggle-card", "--from", "a"]), "bsc ui").is_err(), "id collision refused");
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "get", "settings-toggle-card", "--json", "--pretty"]), "bsc ui").is_ok());
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "list", "--json"]), "bsc ui").is_ok());

        // The stored record is derived, carries its exemplars, and does NOT carry a member list.
        let rec: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(pdir.get("settings-toggle-card").unwrap().unwrap().as_str()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rec["signatureSource"], "derived");
        assert_eq!(rec["exemplars"].as_array().map(Vec::len), Some(3));
        assert!(rec.get("members").is_none(), "membership is computed, never frozen into the record");

        // The reverse lookup, both outcomes.
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "of", "a", "--json"]), "bsc ui").is_ok());
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "of", "ghost"]), "bsc ui").is_err(), "an absent component names itself");
        store.set("chart", &serde_json::json!({
            "id": "chart", "name": "Chart", "kitId": "react-ui", "composes": ["Axis"],
            "srcText": "export const Chart = () => <Axis scale={s}/>;",
        }).to_string()).unwrap();
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "of", "chart"]), "bsc ui").is_ok(), "belonging to none is an answer, not an error");

        // A newly authored sibling is a member with NO edit to the pattern — the point of computing it.
        store.set("new", &card("new", "TelemetryCard").to_string()).unwrap();
        let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
            store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str(j).ok()).collect();
        let members = crate::patterns::conforming(&rec, &comps, true);
        assert!(members.iter().any(|m| m.id == "new"), "the new sibling joined: {:?}", members.iter().map(|m| &m.id).collect::<Vec<_>>());
        assert!(!members.iter().any(|m| m.id == "chart"), "the unrelated record did not");

        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "remove", "settings-toggle-card"]), "bsc ui").is_ok());
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "remove", "settings-toggle-card"]), "bsc ui").is_err(), "removing nothing is an error");
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "--nope"]), "bsc ui").is_err(), "unknown flag");
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "wat"]), "bsc ui").is_err(), "unknown subcommand");
        assert!(run(vec!["pattern".into(), "help".into()], "bsc ui").is_ok(), "help reachable");
        assert!(COMPONENT_COMMANDS.iter().any(|c| c.name == "pattern"), "the verb is documented");
    }

    /// #113: a component genuinely referenced in another's JSX but never added to `composes` reads as
    /// an orphan under `used-by` — `refs` is the srcText scan that tells the two apart.
    #[test]
    fn refs_finds_a_jsx_reference_used_by_cannot_see() {
        let store = tmp_component_store("refs");
        let dir = store.dir().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        for rec in [
            serde_json::json!({
                "id": "widget", "name": "Widget", "kitId": "react-ui", "role": "primitive", "composes": [],
                "srcText": "export const Widget = () => <div />;",
            }),
            // References Widget in JSX, and separately imports it — but never lists it in `composes`.
            serde_json::json!({
                "id": "page", "name": "Page", "kitId": "react-ui", "role": "composite", "composes": [],
                "srcText": "import { Widget } from \"@/x/Widget\";\nexport const Page = () => <Widget />;",
            }),
            // Shares no reference at all.
            serde_json::json!({
                "id": "unrelated", "name": "Unrelated", "kitId": "react-ui", "role": "primitive", "composes": [],
                "srcText": "export const Unrelated = () => <span />;",
            }),
        ] {
            store.set(rec["id"].as_str().unwrap(), &rec.to_string()).unwrap();
        }
        let d = |extra: &[&str]| {
            extra.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).chain(["--dir".to_string(), dir.clone()]).collect::<Vec<_>>()
        };

        // `used-by` sees NOTHING — there is no `composes` edge — which is exactly the false "orphan"
        // #113 filed against. `used-by` itself prints via plain `println!`, so its human output is not
        // capturable here; going straight at the composes-inverse index proves the same fact.
        let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
            store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();
        let idx = used_by_index(&comps);
        assert!(
            !idx.contains_key(&("react-ui".to_string(), "Widget".to_string())),
            "used-by is blind to the JSX reference: no `composes` edge names Widget"
        );

        // `refs` finds it: `page` shows both a JSX hit and an import-clause hit, `unrelated` does not appear.
        let (r, out) = bsc_util::capture_output(|| run(d(&["refs", "widget", "--json"]), "bsc ui"));
        r.unwrap();
        let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(out.trim()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v["name"], "Widget");
        assert_eq!(v["count"], 1);
        assert_eq!(v["refs"][0]["id"], "page");
        assert_eq!(v["refs"][0]["jsx"], 1);
        assert_eq!(v["refs"][0]["importClause"], 1);

        // The text form names the referencer and never mentions `unrelated`.
        let (r, out) = bsc_util::capture_output(|| run(d(&["refs", "widget"]), "bsc ui"));
        r.unwrap();
        assert!(out.contains("Page"), "{out}");
        assert!(!out.contains("Unrelated"), "{out}");

        // A component nothing references at all — the genuinely-dead case `refs` exists to confirm.
        let (r, out) = bsc_util::capture_output(|| run(d(&["refs", "unrelated"]), "bsc ui"));
        r.unwrap();
        assert!(out.contains("no literal srcText reference found"), "{out}");

        assert!(run(vec!["refs".into(), "help".into()], "bsc ui").is_ok(), "help reachable");
        let err = run(d(&["refs", "ghost"]), "bsc ui").unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("no component with id 'ghost'"), "{err}");

        // A READ — in the catalog, never a scoped mutation, and runs under a read-only ui scope.
        assert!(COMPONENT_COMMANDS.iter().any(|c| c.name == "refs"));
        assert!(!is_scoped_mutation(&["refs".to_string(), "widget".to_string()]), "refs is a read");
        bsc_cli_util::with_scopes(Some(r#"{"ui":"read"}"#), || {
            assert!(run(d(&["refs", "widget"]), "bsc ui").is_ok(), "refs works read-scoped");
        });
    }
